children.translated_text: There was a certain merchant.
Near the city he was having a temple of a deity built.

children.text: tatra ye karmakārāḥ sthapatyādayaḥ madhyāhnavelāyām āhāranimittaṃ bhojanamaṇḍapam anupraviṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There the workmen, such as the master builders and others, had entered the dining pavilion at midday for the sake of their meal.
Suddenly, as an incidental occurrence, a troop of monkeys came to the temple.

children.text: atha tatraikasya śilpino 'rdhasphoṭitakāṣṭhastambho 'rjunamayaḥ khadirakīlakena madhye yantranikhātenāvastabdho 'vatiṣṭhate ||
children.translated_text: Now there stood there a carpenter’s pillar of arjuna wood, half split, held fast in the middle by a khadira-wood wedge driven in by the mechanism.

children.text: tatra kadācid vānarayūtho giriśikharād avatīrya svecchayā taruśikharaprāsādaśṛṅgadārunicayeṣu prakrīḍitum ārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then at some time the troop of monkeys came down from the mountain peak and, as they pleased, began to play on the tops of trees, the pinnacles of the temple, and the heaps of timber.

children.text: ekas tu tatrāsannavināśaś cāpalād upaviśya stambhe yantracāram uddiśyedam āha ||
children.translated_text: But one among them, whose destruction was near, sat down on the pillar out of restlessness and, looking at the movement of the mechanism, said this:
“By whom has this wedge been driven in at an improper place?”
So saying, he grasped it with his two hands and began to pull it out.

children.text: sthānāc calite kīle yad vṛttam tad anākhyeyam evam eva bhavatā jñātam iti ||
children.translated_text: When the wedge was moved from its place, what happened is not to be told; you yourself have understood it in just this way.

children.text: asti kaścid gomāyur āhāravicchedāt kṣutkṣāmakaṇṭha itaś ca itaḥ paribhramann ubhayasainyasyāyodhanabhūmim apaśyat ||
children.translated_text: There was a certain jackal whose throat was emaciated with hunger because his food had been cut off; wandering here and there, he saw the battlefield of two armies.
And there he heard a great sound.

children.text: tadbhayasaṃkṣubhitahṛdayaḥ kim idam vinaṣṭo 'smi kasyāyaṃ śabdaḥ kva vā kīdṛśo vaiṣa śabda iti cintayatā dṛṣṭā giriśikharākārā bherī ||
children.translated_text: His heart shaken by fear, he thought, “What is this? I am ruined. Whose sound is this? Where is it, and what kind of sound is this?” Then he saw a drum shaped like a mountain peak.
Seeing it, he reflected:

children.text: kim ayaṃ śabdo 'syāḥ svābhāvikaḥ uta paraprerita iti ||
children.translated_text: “Is this sound natural to it, or is it set in motion by another?”

children.text: atha sā yadā vāyupreritair vṛkṣāgraiḥ spṛśyate tadā śabdaṃ karoti anyadā na iti tūṣṇīm āste ||
children.translated_text: Then, when it was touched by the tips of trees driven by the wind, it made a sound; at other times it did not, but remained silent.

children.text: sa tu tasyāḥ sārāsāratāṃ jñātuṃ saṃnikarṣam upaśliṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: So, in order to know whether it had substance or was without substance, he drew close to it.

children.text: svayaṃ ca kautukād ubhayor mukhayor atāḍayat acintayac ca ||
children.translated_text: Out of curiosity he himself struck both its faces and thought:
“This is accessible, and it is food for me.”
Having decided this, possessed by hunger, he tore it with one fang.

children.text: paruṣatvācca carmaṇaḥ kathamapi na daṃṣṭrābhaṅgam avāptavān ||
children.translated_text: Because the hide was tough, he somehow avoided breaking his fang.
Being obstructed, he again thought:
“Surely there must be food inside it.”

children.text: ity adhyavasya bheryā mukhaṃ vidāryāntaḥ praviṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having resolved this, he split open the mouth of the drum and entered inside.
Even there he obtained nothing at all.
Unable to return, with half his body hidden inside, he laughed and said:
“I knew it from the very beginning.”

children.text: asti kasmiṃścit pradeśe parivrāḍ devaśarmā nāma ||
children.translated_text: In a certain region there was an ascetic named <s>Devaśarman</s>.
From the accumulation of fine garments of special quality provided by many holy men, a great amount of wealth had come into his possession.

children.text: sa ca na kasyacid api viśvāsaṃ yāti ||
children.translated_text: And he did not place trust in anyone at all.

children.text: atha kadācid āṣāḍhabhūtir nāma paravittāpahṛt katham iyam arthamātrāsya mayā parihartavyeti vitarkyāvalaganarūpeṇa upagamya tatkālena ca viśvāsam anayat ||
children.translated_text: Then one day a thief of others’ property named <s>Āṣāḍhabhūti</s> considered, “How can this amount of wealth of his be carried off by me?” and, approaching him in the form of an attendant, in due course gained his trust.

children.text: atha kadācid asau parivrājakas tīrthayātrāprasaṅge tena āṣāḍhabhūtinā saha gantum ārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then at some time that mendicant, in connection with a pilgrimage to sacred fords, began to travel together with that <s>Āṣāḍhabhūti</s>.

children.text: tatra ca kasmiṃścid vanoddeśe nadītīre mātrāntika āṣāḍhabhūtim avasthāpyaikāntam udakagrahaṇārthaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, in a certain part of a forest on the bank of a river, he stationed <s>Āṣāḍhabhūti</s> near his possessions and went aside to fetch water.
And he saw a great fight between two rams.

children.text: anavaratayuddhaśaktisampannayoś ca tayoḥ śṛṅgapañjarāntarodbhūtāsṛg bahu bhūmau nipatitaṃ dṛṣṭvā āśāpratibaddhacittaḥ piśitalobhatayā gomāyus tajjighṛkṣuḥ saṃpīḍitodghātāt sadyaḥ pañcatvam agamat ||
children.translated_text: Seeing much blood fall on the ground from between the cages of the horns of those two, who possessed the power for unceasing battle, a jackal, his mind bound by expectation and greedy for flesh, wished to seize it; from being crushed by their blows, he immediately met the state of death.
Then the ascetic, filled with astonishment, said:
“The jackal by the rams’ fight...”

children.text: kṛtaśaucaś cāgatas tam uddeśam āṣāḍhabhūtim api gṛhītārthamātrāsāram apakrāntaṃ nāpaśyad devaśarmā ||
children.translated_text: Having performed his purification, <s>Devaśarman</s> came back to that place and did not see <s>Āṣāḍhabhūti</s>, who had taken the substance of his wealth and gone away.
He saw only the discarded triple staff, wooden water-pot, strainer, brush, and the like, and he thought:
“Where is that <s>Āṣāḍhabhūti</s>?”
“Surely I have been robbed by him.”
So he said.
“And we by <s>Āṣāḍhabhūti</s>...”

children.text: athāsau kapālaśakalagranthikāvaśeṣaḥ kaṃcid grāmam astaṃ gacchati ravau praviṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, with only a skull fragment and a bundle remaining, he entered a certain village as the sun was setting.

children.text: praviśann ekāntavāsinaṃ tantravāyam apaśyat āvāsakaṃ ca prārthitavān ||
children.translated_text: As he entered, he saw a weaver living alone and asked for lodging.

children.text: tenāpi tasyātmīyagṛhaikadeśe sthānaṃ nirdiśya bhāryā abhihitā ||
children.translated_text: The weaver too assigned him a place in one part of his own house and said to his wife:

children.text: yāvad ahaṃ nagaraṃ gatvā suhṛtsameto madhupānaṃ kṛtvā āgacchāmi tāvad apramattayā gṛhe tvayā bhāvyam ||
children.translated_text: “Until I go to the city, drink liquor together with my friends, and return, you must remain vigilant in the house.”
Having instructed her thus, he went away.

children.text: atha tasya bhāryā puṃścalī dūtikāsaṃcoditā śarīrasaṃskāraṃ kṛtvā paricitasakāśaṃ gantum ārabdhā ||
children.translated_text: Then his wife, a wanton woman, urged on by a female messenger, adorned her body and began to go to her lover’s presence.

children.text: abhimukhaś cāsyā bhartā madavilopāsamāptākṣaravacanaḥ pariskhalitagatir avasrastavāsāḥ samāyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But her husband came toward her, with his words indistinct because of drunkenness, his gait stumbling, and his clothes slipping down.

children.text: taṃ ca dṛṣṭvā pratyutpannamatiḥ kauśalād ākalpam apanīya pūrvaprakṛtam eva veṣam āsthāya pādaśaucaśayanādyārambham akarot ||
children.translated_text: Seeing him, quick-witted, she skillfully removed her adornment, assumed again her former natural dress, and began the preparations for washing his feet, making the bed, and so on.

children.text: kaulikas tu gṛhaṃ praviśya nidrāvaśam agamat ||
children.translated_text: But the weaver entered the house and fell under the power of sleep.
And he, having awakened from sleep, began to abuse her.

children.text: puṃścali tvadgatam apacāraṃ suhṛdo me varṇayanti ||
children.translated_text: "Wanton woman, my friends describe your misconduct to me.
So be it.
I shall impose a severe punishment," he said.

children.text: asāv api nirmaryādā prativacanaṃ dātum ārabdhā ||
children.translated_text: She too, shameless as she was, began to give him an answer.

children.text: punar api cāsau pratibuddhas tāṃ madhyasthūṇāyāṃ rajjvā supratibaddhāṃ kṛtvā prasuptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again he woke up, bound her very tightly with a rope to the central post, and went to sleep.
The female messenger urged her once more to go.

children.text: sā tūtpannapratibhā dūtikām ātmīyadarśanasaṃvidhānena baddhvā kāmukasakāśaṃ yayau ||
children.translated_text: But she, being quick-witted, bound the messenger there in such a way that she looked like herself, and went to her lover's presence.

children.text: asāv api pratibuddhas tathaiva tām ākroṣṭum ārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He too woke up and in the same way began to abuse her.

children.text: dūtikā tu śaṅkitahṛdayānucitavākyodāharaṇabhītā na kiṃcid uktavatī ||
children.translated_text: But the messenger, with a fearful heart and afraid of uttering an improper word, said nothing.

children.text: tantravāyas tu śāṭhyād iyaṃ na kiṃcin mamottaraṃ prayacchati ityutthāya tasyās tīkṣṇaśastreṇa nāsikāṃ chittvābravīt ||
children.translated_text: The weaver, thinking, "Because of her deceit she gives me no answer," got up, cut off her nose with a sharp knife, and said:
"Stay marked in this way.
Who will ask you for news now?"
Having said this, he fell under the power of sleep.

children.text: āgatā ca sā tantravāyī dūtikām apṛcchat ||
children.translated_text: When the weaver's wife returned, she asked the messenger:
"What is your news?
Did he wake up and say anything?
Tell me, tell me."

children.text: dūtikā tu kṛtanigrahā nāsikāṃ darśayantī sāmarṣam āha ||
children.translated_text: But the messenger, having been punished, showed her nose and said angrily:
"All your news is auspicious.
Untie me.
I am going," she said.
When that had been done, she took her nose and went away.
The weaver's wife also made herself appear as if she had been falsely bound.

children.text: kaulikas tu yathāpūrvam eva pratibuddhas tām ākrośat ||
children.translated_text: The weaver, waking up just as before, abused her.

children.text: asāv api duṣṭā bahu dhṛṣṭaram āha ||
children.translated_text: But that wicked woman, with much greater audacity, said:
"Shame on you, wretch!
Who is able to disfigure me when I am innocent?
Let the world-protectors hear me.

children.text: yathāhaṃ kaumāraṃ bhartāraṃ muktvā nānyaṃ parapuruṣaṃ manasāpi vedmi tathā mamānena satyenāvyaṅgyaṃ mukham astviti ||
children.translated_text: Since, after taking my husband in maidenhood, I know no other man, not even in thought, by this truth may my face be without blemish."

children.text: athāsau mūrkhaḥ kṛtakavacanavyāmohitacittaḥ prajvālyolkām avyaṅgamukhīṃ jāyāṃ dṛṣṭvā protphullanayanaḥ paricumbya hṛṣṭamanā bandhavād avamucya pīḍitaṃ ca pariṣvajya śayyām āropitavān ||
children.translated_text: Then that fool, his mind deluded by her feigned words, lit a torch, saw his wife with her face unblemished, and, with eyes wide open, kissed her; delighted in mind, he released her from the bonds, embraced her though she was bruised, and put her on the bed.

children.text: parivrājakas tv ādita evārabhya yathāvṛttam artham abhijñātavān ||
children.translated_text: But the wandering mendicant had understood the matter just as it had happened, from the very beginning.
The messenger too, holding the nostril made by her hand, went to her own house and thought:
"What is to be done now?"

children.text: atha tasyā bhartā nāpito rājakulāt pratyūṣasy āgatya tāṃ bhāryām āha ||
children.translated_text: Then her husband, a barber, came from the royal household at dawn and said to his wife:
"Hand me the razor-case, good woman.
Work has to be done in the royal household."

children.text: sā ca duṣṭābhyantarasthaiva kṣuram eva prāhiṇot ||
children.translated_text: But that wicked woman, staying inside, sent only a razor.

children.text: sa ca samastakṣurabhāṇḍāsamarpaṇāt krodhāviṣṭacitto nāpitas tam eva tasyāḥ kṣuraṃ pratīpaṃ prāhiṇot ||
children.translated_text: And because the whole razor-case had not been handed over, the barber, his mind seized by anger, sent that very razor back toward her.

children.text: athāsāv ārtaravam uccaiḥ kṛtvā pāṇinā nāsāpuṭaṃ pramṛjya asṛkpātasametāṃ nāsikāṃ kṣitau prakṣipyābravīt ||
children.translated_text: Then she raised a loud cry of pain, wiped her nostril with her hand, threw the nose, together with falling blood, onto the ground, and said:
"Protect me! Protect me!
I, innocent of any offense, have been disfigured by this man."

children.text: tathābhyāgatai rājapuruṣaiḥ pratyakṣadarśanāṃ tāṃ dṛṣṭvā virūpāṃ kīlapārṣṇilaguḍair atīva hataṃ paścād bāhubandhaś ca tayā saha dharmasthānam upanīto nāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the king's men arrived in that way, they saw her disfigured before their eyes; after beating the barber severely with pegs, heel-blows, and clubs, they bound his arms behind him and brought him together with her to the court of justice.

children.text: pṛcchyamānaś cādhikṛtaiḥ kim idaṃ mahad viśasanaṃ svadāreṣu tvayā kṛtam iti yadā bahuśa ucyamāno nottaraṃ prayacchati tadā dharmādhikṛtāḥ śūle 'vataṃsyatām ity ājñāpitavantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when, though questioned repeatedly by the officials, "What is this great cruelty you have done to your own wife?", he gave no answer, the officers of justice ordered, "Let him be impaled on a stake."

children.text: niṣpāpaṃ ca parivrāṭ śūlasthānaṃ nīyamānaṃ nāpitaṃ dṛṣṭvā sattvānukampayā copalabdhatattvārtho 'dhikaraṇam upagamya dharmasthānādhikṛtān abravīt ||
children.translated_text: But the wandering mendicant, seeing the sinless barber being led to the place of impalement, and having perceived the true facts, went to the tribunal out of compassion for living beings and said to the officers of the court:
"You ought not to set this barber, who has committed no offense, upon the stake.
For this reason, hear of these three marvels:
The jackal through the rams' fight, and we through <s>Āṣāḍhabhūti</s>;
the messenger through the weaver: these three misfortunes were self-made."
And when the officials had understood the true facts, the barber was saved.

children.text: asti kasmiṃścit pradeśe vṛkṣaḥ tasmiṃś ca vāyasau dampatī prativasataḥ sma ||
children.translated_text: In a certain region there was a tree, and in it lived a pair of crows, husband and wife.

children.text: tayos tu prasavakāle tadvṛkṣavivarānusāryasaṃjātakriyāṇyevāpatyāni kṛṣṇasarpo bhakṣayati sma ||
children.translated_text: At their breeding time, a black snake that kept to the hollow of that tree used to eat their young as soon as they had come into being.

children.text: atha tenāpakāranirvedanād anyavṛkṣamūlavāsinaṃ priyasuhṛdaṃ gomāyum apṛcchyata yathā ||
children.translated_text: Then, distressed by that injury, one of them asked a dear friend, a jackal living at the root of another tree, as follows:

children.text: bhadra kim evaṃgate prāptakālaṃ bhavān manyate ||
children.translated_text: "Good sir, in such a situation, what do you think is timely?
Because our young are being killed, there is no old age for the two of us."
The jackal said:
"After eating many fish, the best, the worst, and the middling,
the heron later died from excessive greed in a fight with a crab."
The crow said:
"How was this?"
The jackal said:

children.text: asti kaścid bako vṛddhabhāvāt sukhopāyāṃ vṛttim ākāṅkṣamāṇaḥ kasmiṃścit saraḥpradeśe 'dhṛtiparītam iva ātmano rūpaṃ pradarśayann avasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There was a certain heron who, because he was old, desired an easy means of livelihood; at a certain place by a lake he remained, displaying himself as though overcome by despondency.
There a crab, surrounded by many fish, said:

children.text: māma kim adyāhārakṛtyaṃ nānuṣṭhīyate yathā pureti ||
children.translated_text: "Uncle, why is the matter of eating not being carried out today as before?"
The crane said:
"I am an eater of fish.
Without deceit on that account, I speak to you.

children.text: mayā yuṣmān āsādya pūrvaṃ prāṇarakṣā kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: Previously, by coming upon you, I protected my life.
Today the severing of my livelihood has arrived.
Therefore I am dejected."
The crab said:
"Uncle, for what reason?"
The crane said:
"Today, as fishermen were passing near this lake, they said:
'This pond has many fish.
Let us cast a net in it.
There are other ponds near the city that have not yet been reached.

children.text: tān āsādya punar āgamiṣyāma iti kathayāmāsuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having reached them, we shall come back again.' So they spoke.
Therefore, my good sir, you are as good as destroyed.
I too, because my livelihood is cut off, am ruined indeed."
Then they entreated him as follows:

children.text: yata evāpāyaḥ śrūyate tata evopāyo 'pi labhyate ||
children.translated_text: "From the very place where danger is heard of, from there a remedy may also be found.
So you ought to save us."
The crane said:
"I am an egg-born creature, powerless against men.

children.text: kiṃtv asmāddhradād anyaṃ jalāśayaṃ yuṣmān saṃkrāmayiṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: But I shall transfer you from this pond to another reservoir."

children.text: tatas tair viśvāsam upagatais tāta bhrātar mātula mātula māṃ naya māṃ naya prathamataraṃ nayasvety abhihitam ||
children.translated_text: Then, having put their trust in him, they said, "Father, brother, uncle, uncle, carry me, carry me, take me first!"

children.text: asāv api duṣṭamatiḥ krameṇa nītvā kauśalād ajasraṃ tān bhakṣayan paraṃ paritoṣam upāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And that evil-minded one, taking them off one by one with skill and eating them continually, reached the highest satisfaction.

children.text: kulīrakas tu mṛtyubhayodvigno muhur muhus taṃ prārthitavān ||
children.translated_text: But the crab, distressed by fear of death, begged him again and again:

children.text: māma mām api tāvad arhasi mṛtyumukhāt paritrātum iti ||
children.translated_text: "Uncle, you should save me too now from the mouth of death."
But that wicked-souled one thought:
"I am weary of this single-flavored fish flesh.
Now I shall taste this one too as a special delicacy."

children.text: tatas samutkṣipya viyat sarvāmbhaḥsthānāni parihṛtyaikadeśe taptaśilāyām avatīrṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, lifting him up into the air and passing by all the watery places, he descended in one spot upon a hot rock.
The crab too, as soon as he saw the heap of bodily remains of fish eaten before, thought:

children.text: nihatā anena durātmanā prajñāpūrvakaṃ te mīnāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Those fish have been deliberately killed by this wicked soul.
So what is timely now?
Or rather:

children.text: abhiyukto yadā paśyen na kāṃcid gatim ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: When a man under attack sees no escape for himself,

children.text: yudhyamānas tadā prājño mriyeta ripuṇā saha ||
children.translated_text: then the wise man should die fighting together with his enemy."

children.text: anabhijño 'pi bakaḥ kulīrakasandaṃśagrahasya maurkhyāt kulīrakasakāśācchiraśchedam avāptavān ||
children.translated_text: The crane, ignorant too of the grip of a crab's pincers, through stupidity had his head cut off by the crab.

children.text: kulīrako 'pi gṛhītvā bakagrīvām utpalanālavad ākāśagamanaprasādhitacihnamārgo matsyāntikam eva prāyāt ||
children.translated_text: The crab, carrying the crane's neck like a lotus stalk, returned through the sky to the fish, his path marked by that journey through the air.
And they said to him:
"Brother, where is that uncle?"
Then he said:
"He has gone to the state of the five elements.
This is the head of that wicked soul.
Many of your own troop were eaten by that deceiver.
He too has perished at my hands."
Therefore I say:
"Having eaten many fish ..."
Then the crow said to the jackal:
"What do you think is timely for the two of us?"
The jackal said:
"Take a golden necklace and place it here in the dwelling.
Without doubt its owner will kill that black snake."
Having said this, the jackal went away.
Then the crow, seeking a golden necklace, went to the royal palace.

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ ca tenāntaḥpuraikadeśe dhautavastrayugalopari suvarṇasūtram uttamamaṇiviracitaṃ mahārhaṃ prakṣālya ceṭikayā sthāpitam ||
children.translated_text: And he saw, in one part of the women's quarters, a very valuable golden necklace set with excellent jewels, washed and placed by a maidservant upon a pair of washed garments.

children.text: tac cāvasthāpyānyayā saha kathāṃ kartum ārabdhā ||
children.translated_text: Leaving it there, she began to converse with another woman.

children.text: vāyasas tu tad gṛhītvā viyatā śanair ātmānaṃ darśayan svam ālayaṃ prati prāyāt ||
children.translated_text: But the crow took it and, slowly showing himself in the sky, went toward his own nest.

children.text: athārakṣipuruṣaiḥ prāsamudgaratomarapāṇibhir mahatā javena gatvā vṛkṣo 'valokitaḥ yāvat tena tat svanīḍe sthāpitam ||
children.translated_text: Then the guards, holding spears, clubs, and javelins, went with great speed and inspected the tree, until they saw that he had placed it in his nest.

children.text: tatraikenārohatā dṛṣṭam kṛṣṇabhujaṅgo vāyasapotān bhakṣayitvā nidrāvaśam agamat ||
children.translated_text: There one man, climbing up, saw that a black serpent, after eating the crow's chicks, had fallen asleep under the power of sleep.
And by him that serpent was killed while still asleep.

children.text: tat kṛtvā suvarṇasūtram ādāya gata iti ||
children.translated_text: Having done that, he took the golden necklace and went away.

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid vanāntare mahān siṃhaḥ prativasati sma ||
children.translated_text: In a certain region of forest there lived a great lion.
He continually made slaughter among the deer and other animals.

children.text: atha te mṛgāḥ sarva evābhimukhāḥ praṇatacittā haritatṛṇāṅkuravaktradhāriṇo 'vanitalāsaktajānavas taṃ mṛgarājaṃ vijñāpayāmāsuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then all those animals approached him directly, with submissive minds, holding fresh green shoots of grass in their mouths, their knees fixed on the surface of the earth, and petitioned that king of beasts:

children.text: bho mṛgarāja kim anena paralokaviruddhena svāmino nṛśaṃsena niṣkāraṇaṃ sarvamṛgotsādanakarmaṇā kṛtena ||
children.translated_text: "O king of beasts, what is the use of this cruel act of slaughtering all the animals without cause, an act opposed to the next world, when it is done by our lord?

children.text: vayaṃ tāvad vinaṣṭā eva tavāpy āhārasyābhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: We, for our part, are already destroyed, and for you too there will be a lack of food.
Thus there is harm to both sides.
So be gracious.

children.text: vayaṃ tu svāmina ekaikaṃ vanacaraṃ vāreṇa svajātisamutthaṃ preṣayāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: We, however, will send to our lord, in turn, one forest creature at a time, arisen from its own species."
When this had been done, in the course of time the hare's turn arrived.
But he, ordered by all the animals, thought with an angry mind:
"This entrance into the mouth of death is the end-maker.
What is timely for me now?"
Or rather, what is impossible for the intelligent?
"I myself shall kill the lion by a stratagem."
Thus, after making him waste his mealtime, he went.

children.text: asāv api kṣutkṣāmakaṇṭhaḥ krodhasaṃraktanayanaḥ sphuradvadanadaśanasaṃgharṣadaṃṣṭrākarālo lāṅgūlāsphālanākārabhayakṛt tam āha ||
children.translated_text: And he, his throat wasted by hunger, his eyes red with anger, terrible with a quivering mouth, grinding teeth, and fangs, and frightening in the way he lashed his tail, said to him:
"What is done to those who are very angry, except the taking of life?
So today you are as good as dead.
What is this delay of yours past the proper time?"
The hare said:
"Master, the passing of the mealtime was not in my own power."
The lion said:
"By whom were you detained?"
The hare said:
"By a lion."
Hearing this, the lion, his heart greatly agitated, said:

children.text: katham anyo 'tra madbhujaparirakṣite vane siṃha iti ||
children.translated_text: "How can there be another lion here in a forest protected by my arms?"
The hare said, "Certainly."
Then the lion reflected:
"What purpose would be served for me by killing this one?
He will show me that rival.
After killing him too, I shall eat this one."
So he said to him:
"Show me that wicked fellow."

children.text: asāv api śaśo 'ntarlīnam avahasya bṛhaspatyuśanasor nītiśāstraṃ pramāṇīkṛtya svārthasiddhaye vimalajalasampannaṃ dvipuruṣaprāpyodakam iṣṭakācitaṃ mahāntaṃ kūpam adarśayat ||
children.translated_text: The hare too, laughing inwardly and taking as his authority the science of policy of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> and <s>Uśanas</s>, for the accomplishment of his own aim showed him a great well, lined with bricks, full of clear water, whose water could be reached by two men.

children.text: asāv apy ātmakāyapratibimbānabhijñatayā kumārgāpannacitto 'yam asau sapatna iti matvā sahasaiva tasya upari saṃnipatito maurkhyāt pañcatvam agamat ||
children.translated_text: And he, because he did not recognize the reflection of his own body, his mind gone onto a wrong path, thought, "This is that rival," and suddenly leapt down upon him; through folly he met his death.

children.text: asti kasyacid rājñaḥ sarvaguṇopetam ananyasadṛśaṃ śayanam ||
children.translated_text: There was the bed of a certain king, furnished with every excellence and unequalled by any other.

children.text: tasmin pracchadapaṭaikadeśe mandavisarpiṇī nāma yūkā prativasati sma ||
children.translated_text: In one part of its coverlet there lived a louse named <s>Mandavisarpiṇī</s>.

children.text: atha tasmiṃṣ ṭiṇṭibho nāma matkuṇo vāyunā preritaḥ saṃnipatitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then a bedbug named <s>Ṭiṇṭibha</s>, driven by the wind, fell upon it.

children.text: sa tu tac chayanam atisūkṣmottaracchadam ubhayopadhānaṃ jāhnavīpulinavipulaṃ paramamṛdu surabhi ca dṛṣṭvā paraṃ paritoṣam upagataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing that bed, with its very fine upper cover, with pillows on both sides, broad as a bank of the <s>Jāhnavī</s>, exceedingly soft and fragrant, he became supremely delighted.

children.text: tatsparśākṛṣṭamanā itaś cetaḥ paribhraman katham api tayā mandavisarpiṇyā sametaḥ ||
children.translated_text: His mind drawn by its touch, wandering here and there, he somehow met that <s>Mandavisarpiṇī</s>.
She said to him:
"From where have you come into this unsuitable dwelling?
Go away from here."
The bedbug said:

children.text: ārye mayā tāvad ihānekaprakārāṇi māṃsāny āsvāditāni brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviṭśūdrāntaḥsthāni rudhirāṇi ca ||
children.translated_text: "Noble lady, I have already tasted many kinds of flesh here, and bloods found inside Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras.

children.text: tāni tu rūkṣāṇi picchilāny atuṣṭikarāṇy amanojñāni ||
children.translated_text: But those are dry, sticky, unsatisfying, and unpleasant.

children.text: yaḥ punar asya śayanasyādhiṣṭhātā tasya manoramam amṛtopamam asṛg bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: But the agreeable, nectar-like blood of the owner of this bed will be different.

children.text: ajasraṃ bhiṣagbhiḥ prayatnād auṣadhādyupakramād vātapittaśleṣmanirodhād anāmayatayā snigdhapeśaladravaiḥ sakhaṇḍaguḍadāḍimatrikaṭukapaṭubhiḥ sthalajajalajakhecarabalavatpradhānapiśitopabṛṃhitair āhārair upacitaṃ rudhiraṃ rasāyanam iva manye ||
children.translated_text: I think his blood, built up by physicians constantly and carefully through treatments with medicines and the like, through restraint of wind, bile, and phlegm, and through foods that keep him healthy, oily, tender, and fluid, seasoned with pieces of sugar, pomegranate, pungent spices, and salt, and strengthened by the chief meats of land animals, aquatic creatures, and birds, is like an elixir.

children.text: tac ca surabhi puṣṭikaraṃ cecchāmy ahaṃ tvatprasādād āsvādayitum iti ||
children.translated_text: And that fragrant and nourishing blood I wish, through your favor, to taste."
Then <s>Mandavisarpiṇī</s> said to him:
"This is impossible for creatures like you, whose mouths are fiery and whose livelihood is biting.
Go away from this bed."
Then he fell at her feet.

children.text: sā tu dākṣiṇyāt tathā nāmeti pratipannā ||
children.translated_text: But she, out of kindness, agreed, saying, "Very well."

children.text: kiṃtu naivākāle na cātimṛdubhāge tvayāsya prahartavyam iti ||
children.translated_text: "But you must not strike him at the wrong time, nor in a very tender place."
He said:
"What is the right time for him?
I do not know, since I am unfamiliar with him."
She explained:

children.text: madhupānaśramāgatanidrasya rativilāsanirbharasuptasya ca śanair mṛdutayā bhavatā vicāraṇīyam ||
children.translated_text: "When he has fallen asleep from the fatigue of drinking wine, or is deeply asleep after the play of love, then you must move about slowly and gently.
A body overcome by intoxication, fatigue, and sleep does not wake quickly."
When this had been settled, at the very first watch of the night he, not knowing the proper time, bit him at the wrong time.

children.text: asāv api pārthiva ulmukadagdha iva saṃlīnakukṣipradeśaḥ sasambhramam utthāyāha ||
children.translated_text: The king, as if burned by a firebrand, with the region of his belly drawn in, rose up in alarm and said:
"Ah, I have been bitten by someone!"

children.text: atha matkuṇaś cakitatvād rājavacanaṃ śrutvā śayanād avatīrya anyad vivaram āśritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the bedbug, frightened on hearing the king's words, got down from the bed and took refuge in another hole.

children.text: śayyāpālair api svāmyādeśāt sunipuṇam anviṣadbhir vastraṃ parivartayadbhir antarlīnā mandavisarpiṇī samāsāditā vyāpāditā ca ||
children.translated_text: But the bed-keepers, at their master's command, searched very carefully, turning over the cloth, and found <s>Mandavisarpiṇī</s> hidden within, and killed her.

children.text: asti kasmiṃścin nagarasamīpe saṃnikṛṣṭavivarābhyantaraśāyī jambukaś caṇḍaravo nāma ||
children.translated_text: Near a certain city there was a jackal named <s>Caṇḍarava</s>, who slept inside a nearby burrow.

children.text: sa kadācid āhāram anveṣamāṇaḥ kṣapām āsādya kṣutkṣāmagalaḥ saṃmīlitalocanaḥ paribhraman nagaraṃ praviṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Once, seeking food, when night had come, with his throat wasted by hunger and his eyes half-closed, he wandered about and entered the city.

children.text: tannagaravāsibhiś ca sārameyais tīkṣṇadaśanakoṭivilupyamānāvayavo bhayabhairavaphetkāraravapūritadigvivara itas tataḥ praskhalan palāyamānaḥ kasmiṃścid ajñānān nīlīkalaśe saṃnipatitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The dogs living in that city, tearing his limbs with the points of their sharp teeth, filled the quarters with terrifying barks; stumbling here and there as he fled, he accidentally fell into a vat of indigo dye.
The pack of dogs went away by the way it had come.
He too, with difficulty, because some span of life remained to him, rose up out of that vat of indigo.

children.text: athāsya taccharīraṃ nīlīrasarañjitaṃ dṛṣṭvā samīpavartinaḥ kroṣṭukagaṇāḥ ko 'yam iti bhayataraladṛśaḥ sarvā diśaḥ pradudruvuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, seeing his body colored with the juice of indigo, the groups of jackals nearby, their eyes trembling with fear and wondering, "Who is this?", fled in all directions.
He too thought:

children.text: nūnam imāṃ svarūpavikṛtiṃ dṛṣṭvaite palāyanta iti ||
children.translated_text: "Surely, seeing this alteration of my appearance, these creatures are fleeing."
Then, keeping a steady mind, he said to them gently:
"Enough of panic.

children.text: aham ākhaṇḍalājñayā sakalaśvāpadakulapālanakṣamaḥ kṣititalam āgata iti ||
children.translated_text: By the command of <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s>, I have come down to earth, capable of protecting the whole race of wild animals."

children.text: atha tadvacanam ākarṇya siṃhavyāghracitrakavānaraśaśahariṇavṛṣadaṃśajambukādayaḥ śvāpadagaṇās taṃ praṇemuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, hearing his words, the groups of wild animals, lions, tigers, leopards, monkeys, hares, deer, wild oxen, gadflies, jackals, and others, bowed down to him.

children.text: pratidinaṃ ca kesarikarajakuliśadāritamattebhapiśitair āpūryamāṇakukṣiḥ kakṣam iva taṃ jambukapūgaṃ bahiḥ kṛtvā siṃhavyāghrādīn āsannavartinaś cakāra ||
children.translated_text: And day after day, with his belly filled with the flesh of rutting elephants torn open by the thunderbolts of lions' claws, he put that pack of jackals outside as if it were straw, and kept the lions, tigers, and others near him.

children.text: ekadā tv asau vividhapiśitanāśitakṣud dikṣu sthitānāṃ kroṣṭukānāṃ krośatāṃ ninādaṃ śrutvā tvaritataram uccair ninanāda ||
children.translated_text: But one day, when his hunger had been destroyed by various meats, he heard the howling sound of jackals standing in the quarters, and very quickly howled loudly.

children.text: atas te siṃhādayas trapayā bhūbhāgadṛṣṭibhājaḥ kaṣṭam aho vañcitāḥ smaḥ kroṣṭāyam ity avadhārya ruṣā taṃ paruṣagiraṃ nāśitavanta iti ||
children.translated_text: Then those lions and the others, looking at the ground in shame, realized, "Alas, we have been deceived; he is a jackal," and in anger destroyed that harsh-voiced creature.

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid vanoddeśe madotkaṭo nāma siṃhaḥ prativasati sma ||
children.translated_text: In a certain region of the forest there once lived a lion named <s>Madotkaṭa</s>.
He had three carnivorous attendants: a leopard, a crow, and a jackal.

children.text: atha tair bhramadbhir dṛṣṭaḥ sārthavāhaparibhraṣṭa uṣṭraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, while wandering, they saw a camel that had strayed from a caravan leader.

children.text: taṃ cājñātapūrvarūpaṃ hāsyajananaṃ dṛṣṭvā siṃhaḥ pṛṣṭavān ||
children.translated_text: Seeing that creature, whose form they had not known before and which caused amusement, the lion asked:

children.text: idam apūrvaṃ sattvam iha vane pṛcchyatām ||
children.translated_text: "This creature, unprecedented here in the forest, should be questioned.
Who are you?"
Then the crow, having learned the true facts, said:
"This is a camel, whose name has been told."
Then, having reassured him, he brought him into the lion's presence.

children.text: tenāpi yathāvṛttam ātmano viyogaḥ sārthavāhāt samākhyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And by him, too, the separation of himself from the caravan leader was related just as it had happened.
The lion gave him protection and a grant of fearlessness.

children.text: evaṃ ca vartamāne kadācit siṃho vanyagajayuddharadanakṣataśarīro guhāvāsī saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: While things were proceeding in this way, once the lion, his body wounded by the tusks in a battle with a wild elephant, became a dweller in his cave.

children.text: pañcaṣaḍdivasātikrānte ca kāle sarva eva ta āhāravaikalyād ātyayikam āpatitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When five or six days had passed, all of them fell into distress because of lack of food.
Since they were exhausted, the lion said to them:

children.text: aham anayā rujā na kṣamaḥ pūrvavad āhāraṃ bhavatām utpādayitum ||
children.translated_text: "Because of this illness, I am not able, as before, to produce food for you.

children.text: te yūyam ātmārthe 'pi tāvad abhyudgamaṃ kuruta ||
children.translated_text: So at least for your own sake, you should go forth."
They said to him:
"Things being so, what concern have we with nourishing ourselves?"
The lion said:

children.text: sādhv anujīvivṛttaṃ madupari bhaktiś ca bhavatām ||
children.translated_text: "Your conduct as dependents is good, and so is your devotion toward me.
What you have said is very excellent.
You are capable, while I am afflicted by sickness.
Therefore bring food for me in this condition."

children.text: yadā ca na kiṃcid ūcuḥ tadā tenābhihitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when they said nothing, he said to them:
"Why this embarrassment?
Search for some creature.

children.text: aham etadavastho 'pi yuṣmākam ātmanaś cotpādayiṣye prāṇayātrārtham iti ||
children.translated_text: Even in this condition I shall produce food for the journey of life, for you and for myself."

children.text: evam uktvā te 'py utthāya saha krathanakena vanāntaraṃ praviṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having been addressed in this way, they also rose up and entered another part of the forest together with <s>Krathanaka</s>.
After setting <s>Krathanaka</s> aside, they began a wicked consultation.
There the crow said:

children.text: vināśitā vayam anena svāminā svādhīne 'py arthe ||
children.translated_text: "We have been ruined by this master, even though the means is in our own power."
The two said:
"How?"
He said:
"Why, this <s>Krathanaka</s>."
They said:
"This one came to us in trust, took refuge with us, and was accepted as a friend."
He said:
"Grass-eaters and flesh-eaters make an unequal connection."
Then the two said:
"This one is protected by the master through his grant of fearlessness.
Therefore this is improper and impossible."
Again the crow said:

children.text: tiṣṭhata yūyaṃ yāvad aham evaitad arthaṃ saṃpratipādayiṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: "Wait, you two, until I myself bring this matter to agreement."
Having said this, he went into the lion's presence.
And the lion said:
"Has some creature been searched out by you?"
The crow said:

children.text: yasya cakṣur balaṃ vā syāt so 'nviṣyatu ||
children.translated_text: "Let one who has eyesight or strength search.

children.text: vayaṃ tu sarva evāhāravaikalyād andhāḥ parikṣīṇaśaktayaś ca ||
children.translated_text: But all of us, because of want of food, are blind and have lost our strength.
Still, at the proper time, you must certainly be informed:
The master has destroyed himself by himself, though the matter was in his own power."
The lion said:
"How?"
The crow said:
"Why, this <s>Krathanaka</s>."
The lion said:
"Alas!
This is cruel.
I have granted him protection and fearlessness as a favor.
Moreover:

children.text: na gopradānaṃ na mahīpradānaṃ na cānnadānaṃ hi tathā pradhānam ||
children.translated_text: Neither the gift of cows, nor the gift of land, nor indeed the gift of food is so important
as people here say the gift of fearlessness is supremely important among all important gifts."
The crow said:
"Ah, what genius the master has for <s>dharmaśāstra</s> (the science of duty)!

children.text: etad anyad api pradhānaṃ maharṣivacanam yathā śreyasām arthe pāpīyān ārambhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is also this other important saying of the great seers: for the sake of better things, an undertaking that is worse may be made.
And it is also said:

children.text: tyajed ekaṃ kulasyārthe grāmasyārthe kulaṃ tyajet ||
children.translated_text: One should abandon one person for the sake of a family; one should abandon a family for the sake of a village.
For the sake of a district one should abandon a village; for one's own sake one should abandon the earth.
And again he said:
"Let the master not kill him himself.
By a stratagem, I have begun his killing."
The lion said:
"How exactly?"
The crow said:

children.text: ayaṃ tāvad etadavasthaṃ svāminam asmāṃś ca dṛṣṭvā svayam ātmānam anyapuṣṭyarthaṃ svargagamanāya sattvahitāya nivedayati ||
children.translated_text: For his part, seeing the master and us in this condition, he offers himself for the sake of nourishing others, for going to heaven, and for the welfare of beings.

children.text: evam abhihitavati vāyase siṃho matibhramam ivārpito na kiṃcid apyudāhṛtavān ||
children.translated_text: When the crow had spoken thus, the lion, as if overcome by bewilderment, said nothing at all.

children.text: asāv api punas tatsakāśaṃ gatvā kṛtakavacanaiḥ pratyekaṃ vijñāpitavān ||
children.translated_text: Then he too went back to them and, with words he had arranged, instructed each one separately.

children.text: siṃhāntikaṃ gatair yuṣmābhir evaṃ vaktavyam iti ||
children.translated_text: "When you have gone into the lion's presence, this is what you must say."

children.text: tataḥ kṛtasaṃvidaḥ saha krathanakena siṃhasakāśaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, after making their agreement, they went with <s>Krathanaka</s> into the lion's presence.
Then the crow bowed and addressed the lion:
"Your Majesty, the master's body must be protected in every way, even with our bodies."
Then he said:
"You have an unsuitable body.

children.text: na yuṣmaccharīropabhoge kṛte 'pyasmākaṃ kiṃcit tṛptikāraṇaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Even if your body were eaten, it would not bring us any satisfaction."
When he had gone away, the jackal said:
"My body is superior to that one of ours.
Therefore let the journey of life be maintained by my life-breaths."
He gave him the very same reply.
And when he too had gone away, the leopard said:

children.text: ābhyāṃ mama viśiṣṭataraṃ śarīram idam upayujyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: "This body of mine is superior to both of theirs; let it be used."
The lion said to him too:
"You too have an unsuitable body."
Hearing this, <s>Krathanaka</s> thought:
"No one here is being killed.

children.text: tad aham apy evam eva bravīmi ||
children.translated_text: So I too will say exactly the same thing."
Then he rose, approached the lion, and said:
"Your Majesty, my body is superior to these.
Therefore let the journey of your life be maintained with my body."

children.text: evam abhivadann eva dvīpigomāyubhyāṃ vidāritobhayakukṣiḥ sadyaḥ pañcatvam upagato bhakṣitaś ceti ||
children.translated_text: Even as he was saying this, his two flanks were torn open by the leopard and the jackal; at once he died and was eaten.
In one region on the shore of the ocean there lived a pair of <s>ṭīṭibha</s> birds.
Once, when the female <s>ṭīṭibhī</s> was about to lay eggs, she said to her husband:
"Find some place where I may give birth."
He said:
"Surely this very place is favorable for increase.
Lay your eggs right here."
She said:
"Enough of this dangerous place.
My offspring will certainly be destroyed by the flooding of the sea-water at high tide."
He said:

children.text: bhadre na śakto mahodadhir mayā sārdham īdṛśaṃ vairānubandhaṃ kartum iti ||
children.translated_text: "Good lady, the great ocean is not able to undertake such enmity with me."
She said:
"Your strength is very unlike the ocean's.
How is one to know the strength or weakness of oneself?
And it is said:

children.text: duḥkham ātmā paricchettum evaṃ yogyo na veti vā
children.translated_text: It is difficult to determine oneself, whether one is fit in this way or not;

children.text: evaṃvid yasya vijñānaṃ saphalās tasya buddhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the purposes of one whose knowledge is of this kind bear fruit.
And moreover:
He who does not welcome the words of friends who desire his welfare

children.text: sa kūrma iva durbuddhiḥ kāṣṭhād bhraṣṭo vinaśyati ||
children.translated_text: perishes, like the foolish turtle fallen from the stick."
The <s>ṭīṭibha</s> said:
"And how is that?"
The <s>ṭīṭibhī</s> said:

children.text: asti kasmiṃścit sarasi kambugrīvo nāma kacchapaḥ prativasati sma ||
children.translated_text: "In a certain lake there once lived a turtle named <s>Kambugrīva</s>.
He had two friends, geese named <s>Vikaṭa</s> and <s>Saṃkaṭa</s>.
Then, through a reversal of the season, a twelve-year drought occurred.
Thereupon the two of them formed this thought:
"This lake has lost its water.
Let us go to another reservoir.

children.text: kiṃ punaś ciroṣitaṃ priyamitraṃ kambugrīvam āmantrayāvahe ||
children.translated_text: But let us first take leave of our dear friend <s>Kambugrīva</s>, with whom we have lived so long."
When they had done so, the turtle said to them:
"Why is leave being taken of me?

children.text: yadi tu sneho 'sti tato mām apy asmān mṛtyumukhāt trātum arhathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If there is affection, then you ought to save me too from this mouth of death.

children.text: yatkāraṇam yuvayos tāvad āhāravaikalyaṃ kevalam asmin svalpodake sarasi mamātra tu maraṇam eva ||
children.translated_text: For the reason is this: for you two there is merely a lack of food in this lake with little water, but for me here there is death itself.
Therefore consider which is heavier, separation from food or separation from a friend."
They replied:
"You speak rightly.
It is so.
But what timely expedient do you know?
We two must certainly carry you.

children.text: tvayā punaś cāpalān na kiṃcid vaktavyam ||
children.translated_text: But because of your fickleness you must not say anything.

children.text: imāṃ tu yaṣṭiṃ madhye daśanair āpīḍaya ||
children.translated_text: Grip this stick in the middle with your teeth.

children.text: evam anayaivoddhṛtya ṣaṣṭimātrāṇi yojanāni mahat saro bhavantaṃ nayāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way, lifting you up with it, we shall carry you sixty yojanas to a great lake.
There we shall live happily."

children.text: evaṃ ca niṣpanne tajjalāśayasaṃnikṛṣṭanagarasyopariṣṭān nīyamānaṃ dṛṣṭvā kim idaṃ śakaṭacakrapramāṇaṃ viyatā nīyata iti janaḥ sakalakalaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When this had been arranged, as he was being carried above a city near that reservoir, people saw him and a great hubbub arose: "What is this, the size of a cartwheel, being carried through the sky?"

children.text: tac ca śrutvāsannavināśaḥ kacchapo yaṣṭiṃ tyaktvābhihitavān ||
children.translated_text: Hearing that, the turtle, whose destruction was near, let go of the stick and said:
"I am a turtle.

children.text: cāpalād eṣa lokaḥ pralapati iti bruvan vacanasamakālam evāśrayāt paribhraṣṭo bhūmau nipatitaḥ māṃsārthinā ca lokena pātasamakālam eva tīkṣṇaśastraiḥ khaṇḍaśo vibhakta iti ||
children.translated_text: This populace is chattering from fickleness." But as he was saying this, at the very moment of speech, he fell from his support, dropped to the ground, and, at the very moment of his fall, was cut into pieces with sharp knives by people eager for meat.

children.text: asti kasmiṃścin mahāhrade mahākāyās trayo matsyāḥ prativasanti sma tad yathā ||
children.translated_text: In a certain great lake there once lived three huge fish, namely:
<s>Anāgatavidhātā</s>, <s>Pratyutpannamati</s>, and <s>Yadbhaviṣya</s>.

children.text: tatrānāgatavidhātrā tadudakāntargatena kadācit tatsamīpe matsyabandhānām atikrāmatāṃ vacanaṃ śrutam ||
children.translated_text: Among them, <s>Anāgatavidhātā</s>, while in that water, once heard the words of fishermen passing nearby.
"This lake has many fish."
"Here we shall make a catch of fish."
And when <s>Anāgatavidhātṛ</s> heard that, he thought:
"They will certainly come.

children.text: tad ahaṃ pratyutpannamatiṃ yadbhaviṣyaṃ ca gṛhītvānyam achinnasrotaskaṃ hradaṃ saṃśrayāmīti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, taking <s>Pratyutpannamati</s> and <s>Yadbhaviṣya</s> with me, I shall resort to another lake whose stream is not cut off."
Then he called those two and asked them about going.

children.text: tatra pratyutpannamatir matinivārito 'bhayacittaḥ kathamapi pramādān nānuyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There <s>Pratyutpannamati</s>, his mind prevented by his own opinion and being without fear, somehow, through negligence, did not follow.

children.text: yadbhaviṣyas tv āsannavināśas tadvacanam anādṛtya nirārambha eva āsīt ||
children.translated_text: But <s>Yadbhaviṣya</s>, whose destruction was near, disregarded his words and simply remained without making any effort.

children.text: anyedyuś cāpayāte 'nāgatavidhātari matsyabandhair antaḥsroto nirudhya prakṣiptaṃ saṃvartajālam ||
children.translated_text: On the next day, when <s>Anāgatavidhātṛ</s> had gone away, the fishermen blocked the inward stream and cast in a surrounding net.

children.text: apakṛṣṭe ca jāle tasmin hrade nāpy ekataro 'vaśiṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when the net was drawn away, not even one fish remained in that lake.

children.text: evaṃ gate pratyutpannamatir mṛtarūpaṃ kṛtvātmānaṃ jalasya upari darśitavān ||
children.translated_text: When matters had gone so, <s>Pratyutpannamati</s> made himself appear dead and showed himself on the surface of the water.

children.text: tair api svayam eva mṛto mahāmatsya iti kṛtvā parisrotasi sthāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They too, thinking, "This large fish is already dead," placed him at the side of the stream.
Leaping up from there, he went to another body of water.

children.text: yadbhaviṣyas tv anekalaguḍaprahārajarjaritaśarīraḥ pañcatvam upanīta iti ||
children.translated_text: But <s>Yadbhaviṣya</s>, his body shattered by many blows from clubs, was brought to death.
Therefore I say:
"<s>Anāgatavidhātṛ</s> and so on."

children.text: atha kadācit prasūtāyāṃ ṭīṭibhyāṃ tadbhartṛjijñāsayā samudreṇa apahṛtās te 'ṇḍakāḥ paśyāmi tāvat ayaṃ kim ārambhata iti ||
children.translated_text: Now once, when the female lapwing had laid her eggs, the ocean, wishing to test her husband, carried off those eggs, thinking, "Let me see what this one will undertake."

children.text: atha ṭīṭibhī śūnyam apatyasthānaṃ dṛṣṭvā paramāvignahṛdayā bhartāram āha ||
children.translated_text: Then the female lapwing, seeing the place for her offspring empty and her heart greatly distressed, said to her husband:
"This is the calamity that has befallen unfortunate me."
He, laughing inwardly, said to her:

children.text: mamāpi tāvat bhadre dṛśyatāṃ sāmarthyam iti ||
children.translated_text: "Good lady, let my power too be seen now."

children.text: tatas tena pakṣisamājaṃ kṛtvā niveditaṃ tadapatyaharaṇajaṃ duḥkham ||
children.translated_text: Then he gathered an assembly of birds and reported the grief born from the theft of his offspring.
There one of them said:
"We are not capable of conflict with the great ocean.
What, then, is timely here?

children.text: sarva eva vayam ākrandena garutmantam udvejayāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: All of us should agitate <s>Garutmant</s> with our lamentation.
He alone will remove our sorrow."
Having decided this, they went to him.

children.text: asāv api devāsuraraṇanimittam āhūto viṣṇunā garuḍas tat svayūthyavyasanaṃ dṛṣṭvā manyum ājagāma ||
children.translated_text: <s>Garuḍa</s> too, though summoned by <s>Viṣṇu</s> on account of the battle between gods and demons, saw the misfortune of his own flock and became angry.

children.text: devo 'pi viṣṇus traikālyadarśanasāmakṣyāt tasyāntargataṃ matvā svayam eva tatsakāśam agamat ||
children.translated_text: The god <s>Viṣṇu</s> also, because of his power of seeing the three times, understood what was within him and went to him himself.
Then, seeing the god, he spoke with his heart still more distressed:

children.text: yuktaṃ tvayā nāthena satā samudrāpasadān mamāyaṃ paribhava iti ||
children.translated_text: "Is it fitting that, when you are my protector, this insult to me should come from the wretch of an ocean?"

children.text: jñātvā ca devaḥ parihasya samudrasyedam uvāca ||
children.translated_text: And the god, understanding, laughed and said this to the ocean:
"Now return the offspring of the lapwing.

children.text: anyathā tvām āgneyāstrapratāpitam anekavaḍavāmukhasahasraparikṣīṇatoyaṃ sadyaḥ kariṣyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise I shall at once make you scorched by a fiery weapon, your waters exhausted by thousands of submarine fire-mouths."
Thus addressed, the great ocean reflected:
"This egg-born one has begun my complete destruction."

children.text: iti matvā praṇamya devaṃ samarpitavān iti ||
children.translated_text: Thinking this, he bowed to the god and returned them.

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid vanoddeśe vṛkajambukakarabhasahito vajradanto nāma siṃhaḥ prativasati sma ||
children.translated_text: In a certain region of forest there once lived a lion named <s>Vajradanta</s>, accompanied by a wolf, a jackal, and a camel.

children.text: kadācid asau vanyadviparadanakoṭipāṭitavakṣā ekadeśasthaḥ kṣutkṣāmatanuḥ kṣudhā parigatān tān sacivān āha ||
children.translated_text: Once, when his chest had been torn by the tips of the tusks of a wild elephant, he remained in one place, his body emaciated by hunger, and said to those ministers, who were oppressed by hunger:

children.text: kiṃcid anviṣyatāṃ vane sattvajātam yenāham etadavastho 'pi bhavatāṃ vṛttim āpādayiṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: "Search in the forest for some living creature, by which, even in this condition, I may provide a livelihood for you."

children.text: atha tadājñāsamakālam eva te 'raṇye paryaṭanto yadā na kiṃcid āseduḥ tadāsau jambukas taṃ śaṅkukarṇanāmānaṃ karabhaṃ vivikte 'bhihitavān ||
children.translated_text: Then, at that very command of his, they wandered in the forest; when they did not obtain anything, that jackal spoke in private to the camel named <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s>:
"What does your honor think is timely here?

children.text: svāmī vajradanto 'smadīyaparyaṭanam anarthakaṃ śrutvā kadācid vināśāya pravartate ||
children.translated_text: When our master <s>Vajradanta</s> hears that our wandering has been fruitless, he may perhaps set about our destruction.

children.text: tad ahaṃ kiṃcid bhavataḥ prārthaye yadi pratīcchasīti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore I ask something of you, if you will agree."
He said:
"Friend, what do I have that can be requested?
Even my body is at your disposal.
Use it as you wish."
Then the jackal said:
"This very thing is the point here.

children.text: ahaṃ te dviguṇaṃ śarīraṃ siṃhasakāśād dāpayiṣye ||
children.translated_text: I shall have the lion give you a body twice as large.

children.text: tvayāpy evaṃ vayam ātmā ca saṃvardhitāḥ syur iti ||
children.translated_text: By this both we and you will be increased."
And he agreed.

children.text: evam abhidhāya siṃhasakāśaṃ gatvā tam āha ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the jackal went to the lion and said to him:
"Master, no living creature has been found.
But this <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s> says:

children.text: bṛhatprasthena dviguṇayā tulayojjāsyaṃ śarīraṃ samprayacchāmi iti ||
children.translated_text: 'I offer my body to be sacrificed on a great scale, with the balance doubled.'"
Hearing that, the lion, delighted, said:
"Let it be done so."

children.text: atha pratipanne śaṅkukarṇaḥ papāta bhūmau khaṇḍaśaś ca kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, when it had been agreed, <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s> fell to the ground and was cut into pieces.

children.text: tataś caturakas taṃ siṃhaṃ rudhiraraktasarvagātraṃ dṛṣṭvā abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Caturaka</s>, seeing that lion with all his limbs stained red with blood, said:

children.text: gacchatu svāmī snānam ācaritum yāvad ahaṃ kravyamukhasahitastiṣṭhāmi ||
children.translated_text: "Let the master go to perform his bath, while I remain here together with <s>Kravyamukha</s>."

children.text: gate ca tasmiṃś caturakas taṃ kravyamukham āha ||
children.translated_text: And when he had gone, <s>Caturaka</s> said to <s>Kravyamukha</s>:

children.text: bhakṣaya tāvad ataḥ piśitam yāvad asau snātuṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Eat some of this meat now, while he has gone to bathe."
He said:
"After eating it, what answer shall I give?"
The jackal said:
"What use is this deliberation of yours?
I shall give the answer for him.

children.text: tvayā punar mama mukham evāvalokitavyam iti ||
children.translated_text: But you must simply look at my face."

children.text: evam ukte tābhyāṃ kravyam atibahu bhakṣitam ||
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the two of them ate a very great deal of the meat.

children.text: atrāntare siṃhaḥ samprāpto yāvat paśyati sakalaṃ jaṭharapiśitam upabhuktam tataś caturakam āha ||
children.translated_text: Meanwhile the lion arrived; when he saw that all the belly-flesh had been eaten, he said to <s>Caturaka</s>:
"Uncle, where is that belly-flesh?"

children.text: evaṃ vadati siṃhe kravyamukho mukhaṃ caturakasyāvalokitavān ||
children.translated_text: When the lion spoke thus, <s>Kravyamukha</s> looked at <s>Caturaka</s>'s face.
<s>Caturaka</s> said:
"Why are you looking at my face now?
Master,
it has been eaten by this one."

children.text: atha siṃhaḥ kuliśakharanakaro bhrūkuṭilamukhaḥ prakaṭitaroṣastaṃ hantum aicchat ||
children.translated_text: Then the lion, whose claws were like thunderbolts, his face twisted in a frown and his anger displayed, wished to kill him.

children.text: athāsāv api vṛko mukhavaivarṇyavepathuvyāptatanur atanupadavikṣepaḥ kṣiprapalāyanapaṭur aṭavīm uddiśya jagāma ||
children.translated_text: Then that wolf too, his body filled with pallor of face and trembling, making long strides and skilled in swift flight, went off toward the forest.
The lion too followed a little way and then turned back.

children.text: etasmiṃś cāntare kathamapi ca tatsamīpam atha kaścit sārthavāho 'nena pathāyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the meantime, somehow, a certain caravan leader came near that place along this road.

children.text: tasya ca sārthāgresaraṃ kaṭāhena galabaddhena karabham āgacchantaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛtakaviṣādo jambukas taṃ siṃham āha ||
children.translated_text: Seeing a camel coming at the head of his caravan with a kettle tied to its neck, the jackal became feignedly despondent and said to that lion:
"Lord, we two are lost.
Let no one at all hold the forest.

children.text: yāvad adyāpi piśitaṃ nopabhujyate tāvad bṛhatprastham ādāya dhanikācāreṇāyaṃ karabhakaḥ samprāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Before the flesh has even yet been eaten, this young camel has arrived in the manner of a creditor, taking a large measure.
So what is timely here?

children.text: gacchatu svāmī digantaram anyat yāvad aham enaṃ labdhacittābhiprāyaṃ karomīti ||
children.translated_text: Let the master go to another quarter, while I make this one understand the intention in my mind."
When this had been said, the lion went away from that place.
<s>Caturaka</s> too ate that flesh for many days.
In a certain region of forest there was a great troop of monkeys.

children.text: sa kadāciddhemantakāle 'sukhāsīno 'tivihvalatayā khadyotaṃ dṛṣṭvāgnir ayam ity āhāryaiḥ śuṣkatṛṇaparṇair ācchādya prasāritabhujaḥ kakṣakukṣivakṣaḥpradeśān kaṇḍūyamānaḥ pratāpamanorathasukhāni kilānubhavati ||
children.translated_text: Once in winter, sitting miserably and greatly distressed, a monkey saw a firefly and thought, "This is fire"; covering it with dry grass and leaves brought for the purpose, stretching out his arms, and scratching the regions of his armpits, belly, and chest, he supposedly enjoyed the pleasures he imagined from its warmth.

children.text: tatraikaḥ śākhāmṛgas tadgatamanā muhurmuhus tam eva mukhenopādhamat ||
children.translated_text: There one branch-animal, intent on that very thing, again and again blew upon it with his mouth.
Then there was one named <s>Sūcīmukha</s>.
He climbed down from a tree and said to him:
"Do not trouble yourself.
This is not fire; this is a firefly."

children.text: athāsāv adhamat tasya tad vacanam avamanyaiva ||
children.translated_text: But that monkey, disregarding his statement, blew on it all the same.

children.text: punaś ca tenāsakṛd vāryamāṇo naiva śāmyati ||
children.translated_text: And though repeatedly restrained by him, he did not stop.

children.text: kiṃ bahunā tāvat tena karṇābhyāśam āgatyāgatya prabalam udvejitaḥ yāvat tena sahasā gṛhītvā śilāyām āvidhya vigataprāṇaḥ kṛto 'sāviti ||
children.translated_text: In short, when that one had come again and again near his ear and greatly irritated him, he suddenly seized him, dashed him against a stone, and made him lifeless.

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne vaṇiksutau suhṛdau staḥ ||
children.translated_text: In a certain town there were two merchant's sons who were friends.
One was <s>Duṣṭabuddhi</s>, "Evil-Minded," and the other was <s>Dharmabuddhi</s>, "Righteous-Minded."
The two went to a certain foreign country for the sake of acquiring wealth.

children.text: atha tatra dharmabuddhir nāmaikaḥ sārthavāhasuto yas tena kasyacit sādhoḥ pūrvasthāpitaṃ kalaśikāgataṃ svabhāgyapracoditaṃ raupyadīnārasahasraṃ prāptam ||
children.translated_text: There a certain caravan leader's son named <s>Dharmabuddhi</s>, impelled by his own fortune, found a thousand silver dīnāras in a small jar, previously deposited by some honest man.

children.text: sa duṣṭabuddhinā saha sampradhārya kṛtārthāv āvāṃ svadeśaṃ gacchāva iti pratyāgatau ||
children.translated_text: After consulting with <s>Duṣṭabuddhi</s>, he said, "We have accomplished our purpose; let us go to our own country," and they returned.
Near the town <s>Dharmabuddhi</s> said:
"Let the dīnāras be divided into half shares.
Let us enter our own houses.
Now we shall live splendidly in the presence of friends, kinsmen, and others."

children.text: atha duṣṭabuddhir antaḥkaṭhinahṛdayaḥ svārthasiddhaye tam āha ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Duṣṭabuddhi</s>, hard-hearted within, said to him for the accomplishment of his own interest:

children.text: bhadra vittaśeṣo yāvad āvayoḥ sāmānyaḥ tāvad avicchinnaḥ snehasadbhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Good sir, so long as the remainder of the wealth is held in common by us two, so long the reality of our affection will remain unbroken.

children.text: kiṃtv ekam ekaṃ śataṃ gṛhītvā praviśāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But let us each take one hundred and enter.

children.text: yatkāraṇam puṇyaparīkṣā hrāsavṛddhibhyāṃ bhaviṣyaty ekārthatā ca janaspṛhaṇīyā ||
children.translated_text: For the testing of merit will occur through decrease and increase, and common ownership will be something people desire."

children.text: tathā cānuṣṭhite śeṣaṃ kutracit suguptaṃ kṛtvā praviṣṭau ||
children.translated_text: When this had been done accordingly, they made the remainder well hidden somewhere and entered.

children.text: atha tadvarṣābhyantare duṣṭabuddhir asadvyayavyasanitvād bhāgyacchidratayā ca kṣīṇapratyaṃśaḥ punar api ca nidhito dharmabuddhinā sahāparaśataṃ vibhaktavān ||
children.translated_text: Then within that year, because <s>Duṣṭabuddhi</s> was addicted to improper expenditure and because his fortune had a hole in it, his own share was exhausted; again he divided another hundred from the deposit together with <s>Dharmabuddhi</s>.
That too was exhausted in the same way within the second year.
When matters had gone thus, <s>Duṣṭabuddhi</s> thought:

children.text: yadi punaḥ śatavibhāgena vibhajāvaḥ tat kiṃ mayā kṛtaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: "If we again divide it by hundreds, then what will I have done?
By stealing the remaining six shares I shall obtain everything."

children.text: evaṃ matvaikākī bhūtvā tām arthamātrām apanīya pradeśaṃ samīkṛtya māsātikrānte kāle dharmabuddhim abhihitavān ||
children.translated_text: Thinking thus, when he was alone he took away that whole amount of money, leveled the place, and, after a month had passed, said to <s>Dharmabuddhi</s>:
"Good sir, make an equal division of the remaining wealth."

children.text: pratipanne ca dharmabuddhinā saha gatvā tam evoddeśaṃ khātakarma kartum ārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Dharmabuddhi</s> agreed, he went with him to that very spot and began the work of digging.

children.text: khanyamāne ca yadā na dṛśyate tadā prathamataraṃ dhṛṣṭatayā duṣṭabuddhiḥ pāṣāṇenātmanaḥ śiro 'tāḍayad abravīc ca sasambhramam ||
children.translated_text: And when, as they dug, it was not seen, then first of all <s>Duṣṭabuddhi</s>, with impudence, struck his own head with a stone and said in agitation:
"Where is that heart of a brahmin, <s>Dharmabuddhi</s>?"
"Surely it has been stolen by you."
Thus, disputing with mutual suspicion, the two went to the seat of justice.
And when that matter had been reported and understood, they were detained because the obscure lawsuit was hard to decide.
Within five nights, <s>Duṣṭabuddhi</s> promised the appointed officials:
"I have witnesses here for the lawsuit concerning the dīnāras."
But when he was questioned by them for the settlement of the lawsuit:
"Who is your witness?
Show him,"
he said:

children.text: yasyaiva vṛkṣasyādhastāt sthāpitaṃ dravyam tenaiva vibhāvayāmi iti ||
children.translated_text: "By the very tree under which the money was placed, I shall prove it."

children.text: atha te vismayam upagatāḥ kathaṃ vanaspatir mantrayiṣyatīti ||
children.translated_text: Then they were amazed: "How will a tree speak counsel?"
After sureties had been taken, the two were dismissed to their homes.
Then <s>Duṣṭabuddhi</s>, having gone to his house, said to his father:
"Father, those paṇas are in my hands.
But they remain bound only by words.

children.text: ahaṃ tu tvām adya rātrau vṛkṣavivare 'smin sthāpayāmi ||
children.translated_text: Tonight I shall place you in this hollow of the tree.
In the morning, when you are questioned in the presence of the judges, prove that he took it."
Then his father said to him:
"Son, we are ruined.
Why? This is no proper means.
And so:

children.text: upāyaṃ cintayet prājño hy apāyam api cintayet
children.translated_text: A wise man should consider a stratagem, but he should also consider its danger;
while the foolish crane was watching, his children were eaten by mongooses."
He said:
"How was that?"
The other said:

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid arjunavṛkṣe bakadampatī prativasataḥ sma ||
children.translated_text: "In a certain arjuna tree there once lived a pair of cranes.

children.text: tatra ca vṛkṣavivarānusārī mahākāyo 'hir asaṃjātakriyāṇy eva apatyāni bhakṣayati sma ||
children.translated_text: There, a great-bodied snake that followed the hollow of the tree used to eat their offspring before they had even grown active.

children.text: tena ca nirvedena naṣṭasaṃjñāv āhārakriyām utsṛjya jalāśayaikadeśe vimanaskāv āsāte ||
children.translated_text: Because of that despair, having lost their senses and given up the act of feeding, they sat dejected in one part of a pond.
Then a certain crab there said to him:
"Uncle, why is food still not being taken today?"
The crane said:
"For me, overcome by distress, how can there be any desire for food?"
Then he said:
"From what kind of cause has this distress arisen?"

children.text: sa tu tasmai yathāvṛttam apatyabhakṣaṇam ākhyātavān ||
children.translated_text: So the crane told him, just as it had happened, about the devouring of his children.
But the crab encouraged him:
"I shall tell you a means for killing it.

children.text: yeyaṃ nakulavasatir etatprabhṛtyavicchinnaparamparayā matsyapiśitaṃ prakīryatām yāvatsarpavasatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: From this mongoose dwelling onward, scatter fish-flesh in an unbroken line all the way to the snake dwelling.
Then those very mongooses will kill it."

children.text: tathā cānuṣṭhite nakulaiḥ piśitamārgānusāribhiḥ pūrvavairakriyām anusmaradbhiḥ khaṇḍaśo 'hiṃ kurvadbhiḥ pūrvadṛṣṭamārgam ādhāvadbhir bakāvāsaṃ gatvā bakasya śeṣāpatyabhakṣaṇaṃ kṛtam iti ||
children.translated_text: When this was done, the mongooses followed the trail of flesh, remembered their former enmity, cut the snake to pieces, and then, rushing along the path they had first seen, went to the cranes’ dwelling and ate the crane’s remaining offspring.
Therefore I say:

children.text: upāyaṃ cintayet prājño hy apāyam api cintayet ||
children.translated_text: A wise man should consider a stratagem, but he should also consider its danger."

children.text: iti bruvann api tenāsau nītvā sthāpito vṛkṣavivare ||
children.translated_text: Even as he was saying this, he was led by him and placed in the hollow of the tree.

children.text: atha prabhātasamaye 'dhikaraṇaprakṛtipratyakṣaṃ dharmaśāstravacanābhiśrāvitena vanaspatinā yathāprastutam abhihitam ||
children.translated_text: Then in the morning, before the court officials themselves, the tree, after being made to hear statements from the law books, declared the matter as presented:
"The money was stolen by <s>Dharmabuddhi</s>."
Hearing that, <s>Dharmabuddhi</s> thought:
"How can a speechless tree utter speech?
There must be some cause here.
By all means this can be solved by intelligence."
Then he said to the judges:
"Ah, what a wonder!

children.text: adyāpy avipluta eva loke dharmabuddhir ahaṃ vijane 'smin vana ekākyāgamya tad dravyaṃ gṛhītavān ||
children.translated_text: Even now, with my sense of <s>dharma</s> unshaken in the world, I came alone to this lonely forest and took that money.
Then I saw an enormous snake coming.
And I thought:
This hardship has befallen me.
And it has been said:

children.text: punar api viṣayā labhyante na tu prāṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Objects of enjoyment may be obtained again, but not life.
I shall come back again.
So I left it here at the very root of the tree.
Now, by royal authority, it must certainly be handed over.

children.text: kiṃtvasmāt sthānād ekānte 'vasthānaṃ kurudhvam yāvad aham enaṃ nidhipālaṃ kṛṣṇasarpaṃ parājayāmi ||
children.translated_text: But stand apart from this place in seclusion until I overcome this black snake, the guardian of the treasure."

children.text: ity uktvāhāryaiḥ śuṣkadāruparṇanicayair vṛkṣavivaram āpūryāgnim ādīpayitum ārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having said this, he filled the hollow of the tree with dry wood and heaps of leaves that had been brought, and began to kindle a fire.

children.text: duṣṭabuddhis tv adhomukhenākṣṇā vilokya vṛkṣavivarāntargataṃ vaṇikputraṃ dṛṣṭvā vyathitamanā abhavat ||
children.translated_text: But <s>Duṣṭabuddhi</s>, looking downward with his eye, saw the merchant’s son inside the hollow of the tree and became distressed in mind.

children.text: pradīpte ca vahnau samantata ujjvalībhūtād vṛkṣavivarāt sphaṭitatanuḥ pluṣṭakeśaḥ srastatvag yadā jāto vaṇik tadā bhūmau nipatitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when the fire had been kindled, and the merchant emerged from the hollow of the tree blazing all around, his body split open, his hair scorched, and his skin hanging loose, he fell to the ground.

children.text: tat tu mahad vaikārikaṃ dṛṣṭvā kim idam iti paraṃ vismayam upagatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing that great and strange transformation, they were utterly amazed and said, "What is this?"

children.text: kiṃcijjīvitaṃ ca pratyakṣam abhijñāya vaṇikputraṃ papracchuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Recognizing directly that a little life still remained, they questioned the merchant’s son:

children.text: kim idam īdṛśam agnipatanam adhyavasitaṃ bhavateti ||
children.translated_text: "Why did your honor undertake such a fall into fire as this?"
Then he said:

children.text: anena duṣputreṇāham avasthām imāṃ prāpita iti ||
children.translated_text: "I have been brought to this condition by this wicked son."
Saying this, he died.
Immediately afterward, the judges, understanding the matter, said:
"This sinful <s>Duṣṭabuddhi</s> should be impaled on a stake."
In a certain town there was a merchant’s son whose relatives had dwindled away.
He set out for another country for the sake of acquiring wealth.
He had a balance made of a thousand palas of iron.

children.text: so 'nyasmin vaṇikputrake tāṃ nikṣipya deśāntaram arthopārjanāya prāyāt ||
children.translated_text: Having deposited it with another merchant’s son, he went to another country to acquire wealth.

children.text: kṣīṇabhāgyatvāc ca tena bahunāpi kālena na kiṃcid āsāditam ||
children.translated_text: But because his fortune had waned, even after a long time he obtained nothing.

children.text: pratyāgataś ca tāṃ tulāṃ tasmāt prārthitavān ||
children.translated_text: When he returned, he asked that man for the balance.
And the other said:
"It has been eaten by mice."
Then he thought:
"This is astonishing.
How will mice eat a balance made of a thousand palas of iron?"

children.text: antarlīnam avahasyābravīt avaśyam etad evam yatkāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: Hiding his laughter within, he said, "Surely this is exactly so, because:

children.text: vṛṣyaṃ svādu mṛdu ca lohaṃ katham ākhavo na bhakṣayiṣyanti iti pratipannavāk ||
children.translated_text: Since iron is strengthening, sweet, and soft, how would mice not eat it?" Thus he accepted the statement.

children.text: asāv api suparihṛṣṭahṛdayaḥ pādyādipuraḥsarāṃ tasya pūjāṃ kartum ārabdhavān bhojane ca prārthitavān ||
children.translated_text: The other too, with his heart greatly delighted, began to perform hospitality for him, preceded by water for the feet and the like, and invited him to a meal.
And not far from his house there was a river.

children.text: tatra snānābhyudyatasya ca tasya svīyaṃ putram ekam āmalakasnānaśāṭikāsametaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ preṣitavān ||
children.translated_text: When that man was getting ready to bathe there, he sent his own son after him, together with an āmalaka and a bathing cloth.

children.text: asāv api pratyāgacchan dārakam anyasmin mitragṛhe suguptaṃ kṛtvā praviṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the other, on his way back, put the boy well hidden in another friend’s house and entered.

children.text: atha bhojanasamaye sārthavāho dārakam adṛṣṭvā samākulamanāḥ śaṅkitahṛdayaś ca tam apṛcchat ||
children.translated_text: Then at mealtime the caravan-leader, not seeing the boy, with his mind agitated and his heart suspicious, asked him:
"Where is that boy who was sent after you?
He has not come in here."
Then he said:
"He was carried off by a hawk."

children.text: tac chrutvā paramāvigno nirdayībhūtaś ca taṃ bāhau gṛhītvā dharmasthānaṃ nītavān āha ca ||
children.translated_text: Hearing that, extremely distressed and made pitiless, he seized him by the arm, led him to the court of justice, and said:
"Protect me!

children.text: anena me dārakaḥ kvāpi gopita iti ||
children.translated_text: My boy has been hidden somewhere by this man."
And he was questioned by the judges:
"What is this?
Let it be told."
He laughed and said:
"He was carried off by a hawk."
Then they, their minds astonished, said to him:
"How could a hawk carry off a boy?"
Being asked the truth by the officers of justice, he said:
"What is strange here?

children.text: yatra tulā lohasahasrasyāsya gehe madīyā mūṣakair bhakṣitā tatra kathaṃ dārakaḥ śyenena nāpahriyata iti ||
children.translated_text: Where my balance of a thousand palas of iron was eaten by mice in this man’s house, how would a boy not be carried off by a hawk there?"

children.text: tacca śrutvā pratipāditavantas te prāḍvivākāḥ parasparasya tattulātaddārakadānam iti ||
children.translated_text: Hearing that, those judges caused each to hand over the balance and the boy belonging to the other.

children.text: asti dākṣiṇātye janapade mihilāropyaṃ nāma nagaram ||
children.translated_text: In a southern country there is a city named <s>Mihilāropya</s>.
Not far from it was a lodging place for mendicants.

children.text: tatra parivrāḍ jūṭakarṇo nāma prativasati sma ||
children.translated_text: There lived a wandering ascetic named <s>Jūṭakarṇa</s>.

children.text: sa bhikṣāvelāyāṃ tasmān nagarāt tīrthabhūta iti brāhmaṇagṛhebhyaḥ sakhaṇḍaguḍadāḍimagarbhāṇāṃ snigdhadravapeśalānām annaviśeṣāṇāṃ bhikṣābhājanaṃ paripūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tam āvasatham avagamya yathāvidhi vratakālaṃ kṛtvā tatra śeṣam āpotake suguptaṃ kṛtvā nāgadantake sthāpayati ||
children.translated_text: At the time for alms, from that city, regarded as a sacred place, he would fill his alms-bowl from the houses of Brahmins with special kinds of food containing pieces of jaggery and pomegranate seeds, rich with oily liquid and soft; then, having returned to that lodging and performed his vow-observance at the proper time, he would put the remainder well hidden in a small hanging pot and place it on a peg.
I live from that, together with my retinue.

children.text: evaṃ bhakṣyamāṇe tasmin suprayatnasthāpite 'pi nirviṇṇaḥ sthānāt sthānam uccair matprati bhayāt saṃkramayati ||
children.translated_text: When it was being eaten in this way, though placed with great care, he became dejected and, out of fear of me, kept moving it high from place to place.

children.text: tad apy aham anāyāsena prāpnomi bhakṣayāmi ca ||
children.translated_text: Even that I obtain without effort and eat.

children.text: athaivaṃ gacchati kāle kadācit tasya parivrāḍ bṛhatsphiṅnāma prāhuṇaka āgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Now as time passed in this way, one day a guest of his, a wandering ascetic named <s>Bṛhatsphiṅ</s>, arrived.

children.text: sa jūṭakarṇas tasya svāgatādyupacāraṃ kṛtvā kṛtayathocitavratakālas tasminn āpotake śeṣaṃ suguptaṃ kṛtvā khaṭvāsīnaḥ śayanagataṃ bṛhatsphijam apṛcchat ||
children.translated_text: That <s>Jūṭakarṇa</s>, after performing the courtesies of welcome and so on for him and carrying out the proper vow-observance at the proper time, put the remainder well hidden in that small hanging pot; then, seated on a bed, he asked <s>Bṛhatsphiṅ</s>, who had lain down:
"You were separated from me from here.

children.text: tata ārabhya keṣu deśāntareṣu tapovaneṣu vā paribhrānta iti ||
children.translated_text: From then on, in what foreign countries or ascetic groves have you wandered?"
He related:

children.text: atha kadācid ahaṃ mahākārttikyāṃ mahātīrthavare puṣkare snānaṃ kṛtvā mahato janasamūhadoṣād bhavatā viyuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Once, at the great Kārttikā festival, after bathing at the excellent great tīrtha of <s>Puṣkara</s>, I was separated from you because of the fault of a great crowd of people.

children.text: tato 'haṃ gaṅgādvāraprayāgavārāṇasyādiṣv anukūlapratikūlaṃ jāhnavīm anu paryaṭan kiṃ bahunā kṛtsnaṃ mahīmaṇḍalaṃ samudraparyantam avalokitavān ||
children.translated_text: After that, wandering along the <s>Jāhnavī</s>, with favorable and unfavorable circumstances, at <s>Gaṅgādvāra</s>, <s>Prayāga</s>, <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, and other places, in short, I saw the whole circle of the earth as far as the ocean."

children.text: ardhākhyāte ca tasmiñ jūṭakarṇaḥ parivrāṇ nāgadantopaśliṣṭo muhurmuhur jarjaram avādayat ||
children.translated_text: But when this had been half told, the wandering ascetic <s>Jūṭakarṇa</s>, leaning against the peg, repeatedly made a rattling sound.

children.text: kathyamānavighne ca kriyamāṇe kupito bṛhatsphig āha ||
children.translated_text: And when an interruption was being made in the story as it was being told, <s>Bṛhatsphiṅ</s>, angered, said:

children.text: aham ādṛto bhūtvā bhavataḥ kathayāmi bhavatas tu kimartham anādaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Having been treated with respect, I am telling you my story; but why is there disrespect on your part?
And so:
Insult, recounting another’s misconduct, diversion to another story, lack of wonder at what is said,

children.text: na dṛṣṭidānaṃ kṛtapūrvanāśanaṃ viraktabhāvasya narasya lakṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: not giving one’s gaze, and undoing former kindness: these are the marks of a man whose affection has faded."
He said:
"Good sir, you should not be angry.
