children.text: paśya ayaṃ me mūṣako mahato 'pakārān karoti bhikṣābhājanapradhvaṃsān na cāham enaṃ śaknomi nivārayitum ||
children.translated_text: Look, this mouse of mine does me great injuries by destroying my alms-bowl, and I am not able to keep him away."
He said:

children.text: kim eṣa ekako 'tra mūṣakaḥ utānye 'pi mūṣakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Is this mouse here alone, or are there other mice too?"
He said:
"What need is there of other mice?
This wicked fellow, like a yogin, constantly deceives me."
Hearing that, the other said:

children.text: jūṭakarṇa na mūṣakamātrasyedṛśī śaktir bhavati kiṃ tarhi kāraṇenātra bhavitavyam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jūṭakarṇa</s>, a mere mouse does not have such power; rather, there must be some cause here.
And it has been said:
Not without reason does mother <s>Śāṇḍilī</s> sell sesame seeds for sesame seeds.

children.text: luñcitāṃl luñcitair ava kāryam atra bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Here there will be some business involving hulled seeds in exchange for hulled seeds.
<s>Jūṭakarṇa</s> said:
How is that?
He said:

children.text: asti ahaṃ kadācid abhyarṇāsu varṣāsu kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne sthitigrahaṇanimittaṃ kaṃcid brāhmaṇam āvāsaṃ prārthitavān ||
children.translated_text: Once, when the rains were near, I asked a certain brahmin in a certain town for lodging, in order to stay there.

children.text: varṣāsv atītāsu punar vihārārthaṃ praharaśeṣāyāṃ śarvaryāṃ pratibuddho 'cintayam ||
children.translated_text: When the rains had passed, I awoke in the last watch of the night in order to go wandering again, and thought:
By which quarter should I go?

children.text: atha yugapad asāvapi brāhmaṇas tasyāṃ velāyāṃ pratibuddho jālakāntaritāṃ bhāryām apṛcchat ||
children.translated_text: Then, at the same time, that brahmin too awoke at that hour and questioned his wife, who was separated from him by a window screen:
Brahmin woman, listen.
Tomorrow will be a festival day.

children.text: tatra tvayā yathāśakti brāhmaṇabhojanaṃ kartavyam iti ||
children.translated_text: On that occasion you must feed brahmins according to your ability.
She replied in speech full of many harsh syllables:
How can you, who are utterly poor, have the means for feeding brahmins?

children.text: evam ukto 'sau kūpe prakṣipta iva na vacaḥ kiṃcid avocat ||
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, he, as if thrown into a well, did not say a single word.
After a long while he spoke again:

children.text: brāhmaṇi kartavyaḥ sañcayo nityaṃ na tu kāryo 'tisañcayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Brahmin woman, savings should always be made, but excessive hoarding should not be done.
This jackal, devoted to excessive hoarding, was killed by a bow.
She said:
How is that?
The brahmin said:
In a certain town there was a hunter who lived by meat.

children.text: sa pratyuṣasy utthāya kiṃcid vanam anupraviśya śīghram eva mṛgaṃ viddhvā kṛtamāṃsasañcayaḥ pratyāgacchan mahati tīrthāvatāre avataran mahiṣaśāvatulyam uddhṛtaviṣāṇaṃ kardamapiṇḍāvaliptagātraṃ sūkaram apaśyat ||
children.translated_text: Rising at dawn, he entered a certain forest, quickly shot a deer, made a store of meat, and, while returning, as he descended at a large ford, he saw a boar like a young buffalo, with tusks raised and body smeared with lumps of mud.
Seeing it, and urged on by an evil omen, he became afraid.

children.text: pratinivṛtya ca pratibaddhagatiḥ sūkareṇa māṃsaṃ saṃkocitakaṃ bhūmau prakṣipya dhanuḥ sa śaraṃ ca kṛtvedam uvāca ||
children.translated_text: Turning back, with his path blocked by the boar, he set down the bundled meat on the ground, strung his bow and arrow, and said this:

children.text: na me dhanur nāpi ca bāṇasaṃdhanaṃ kim eṣa śaṅkāṃ samupaiti sūkaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Neither my bow nor the setting of my arrow gives cause for fear; why does this boar fall into suspicion?

children.text: prasahya paśyāmy aham asya niścayaṃ yamena nūnaṃ prahito mamāntikam ||
children.translated_text: I shall forcibly see his resolve; surely he has been sent by <s>Yama</s> to me.

children.text: ity uktvā tasmai viṣadigdham iṣuṃ prāhiṇoj jatrusthāne viddhvā parapārśvagataṃ ca kṛtavān ||
children.translated_text: Having said this, he sent a poison-smeared arrow at him, struck him at the collarbone, and made it pass out the other side.

children.text: sūkareṇāpi prahāramūrchitenottamaṃ javam āsthāyāvaskarapradeśe tathābhyāhataḥ yena gatāsus tridhāgataśarīro nipatitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But the boar too, stunned by the blow, took up the highest speed and struck him in the waste place so that, his life gone and his body split in three, he fell down.

children.text: atha tasmin mahati viṣame vṛtte mṛgalubdhakasūkaraprastare kṣutkṣāmakukṣir dardurako nāma gomāyur āhārārthī tam uddeśam āgato 'paśyan mṛgasūkaralubdhakān ||
children.translated_text: Then, when that great and terrible event had occurred, in the heap of deer, hunter, and boar, a jackal named <s>Darduraka</s>, his belly thin with hunger and looking for food, came to that place and saw the deer, the boar, and the hunter.

children.text: tāṃś ca dṛṣṭvā paraṃ paritoṣam upāgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing them, he was filled with the greatest delight.
And he said:
Food and drink do not constantly arise for embodied beings.
Having obtained abundant food to eat, one should use it up gradually.
So he spoke.
Having said this, he began to eat the bowstring.

children.text: kathamapi daivāc chinne pratibandhe vakṣaḥpradeśe bhinnaḥ pañcatvam upagata iti ||
children.translated_text: Somehow, by fate, when the string was cut, he was pierced in the region of the chest and died.
Therefore I say:
Savings should always be made.
So, brahmin woman, life is lived by plain frugality.
Hearing that, the brahmin woman said:
I have a small amount of sesame seeds and a small amount of rice.

children.text: sa tvaṃ pratyuṣasy utthāya samitkuśādyānayanārthaṃ vanaṃ gaccha ||
children.translated_text: So you rise at dawn and go to the forest to bring fuel, kuśa grass, and the like.

children.text: aham api sahānena śiṣyeṇa kāmandakinā brāhmaṇatrayasya sādhayiṣyāmi kṛsaram iti ||
children.translated_text: I, together with this pupil <s>Kāmandaki</s>, will prepare kṛsara for three brahmins.
When that had been done, a prastha of sesame seeds was set down under <s>Kāmandaki</s>'s supervision with the instruction, 'Husk them.'

children.text: tathā cātivyagratvāt te tilāḥ kathamapi daivāc chunā viṭvālitāḥ tayā cābhyantarasthayā dṛṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: But because of excessive busyness, those sesame seeds were somehow, by fate, defiled by a dog, and she, being inside, saw them.
Then she said:
<s>Kāmandaka</s>, something bad has happened.
An obstacle has arisen to the feeding of the brahmins.

children.text: tathāpi gaccha imāṃs tilāṃlluñcitān api kṛṣṇatilaiḥ parāvartayitvā śīghram āgaccha ||
children.translated_text: Still, go and exchange these sesame seeds, even though they are hulled, for black sesame seeds, and come back quickly.
I shall make black kṛsara instead.

children.text: tathā cānuṣṭhite yasmin veśmany ahaṃ bhikṣārtham upāgataḥ tasminn eva kāmandakir api tilavikrayārtham anupraviṣṭo 'kathayat ||
children.translated_text: When that had been done, in the very house where I had come for alms, <s>Kāmandaki</s> too entered to sell the sesame seeds and said:
Let these sesame seeds be taken.
The brahmin woman said to him:
How are the sesame seeds being given?
<s>Kāmandaki</s> said:

children.text: śuklān kṛṣṇaiḥ prayacchāmi yadīṣṭaṃ gṛhyatām iti ||
children.translated_text: I give white ones for black ones; if you wish, take them.

children.text: tatheme luñcitā bhadre luñcitān eva dehi me ||
children.translated_text: Good lady, thus give me hulled seeds in exchange for hulled seeds.
When this was happening, her husband arrived.
He said:
Good lady, what is this?
She said to him:

children.text: samārghās tilā mayā labdhāḥ śuklāḥ kṛṣṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: I have obtained sesame seeds of equal value, white ones for black ones.
Then he laughed and said:
Not without reason does mother <s>Śāṇḍilī</s> sell sesame seeds for sesame seeds.
She gives hulled seeds only for hulled seeds; there must be some cause here.
So it was.
Having told this story, the wandering ascetic said:
Is there some digging tool?
<s>Jūṭakarṇa</s> said:
"Certainly there is."

children.text: upanīte ca tasmin kakṣyāṃ baddhvā saṃdaṣṭauṣṭhapuṭaḥ pṛṣṭavān ||
children.translated_text: And when he had been brought near, he bound him in a corner and, with his lips clenched between his teeth, questioned him:
"Which is his path of movement?"

children.text: ākhyāte ca tasmin khātakarma kartum ārabdhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When it had been pointed out, he began the work of digging.

children.text: ahaṃ cādāv eva tayor ātmagatam ālāpaṃ śrutvāharam utsṛjya kautukaparo 'vasthita āsam ||
children.translated_text: And I, having heard the private conversation of those two from the very beginning, had left my food and remained there out of curiosity.

children.text: yadā tv asau durgānveṣaṇaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ tadā mayā jñātam ||
children.translated_text: But when that man began to search for my fortress, then I understood:
"This wicked man has discovered the entrance to my hole."

children.text: mayāpi kenāpi sādhunā pūrvasthāpitaṃ suvarṇam āptam āsīt ||
children.translated_text: I too had obtained gold that had previously been deposited by some good man.

children.text: tat prādhānyāc cāhaṃ śaktimantam ātmānaṃ manye ||
children.translated_text: Because of its importance, I considered myself powerful.

children.text: asāv api duṣṭo vivarānusārāt tad upalabhya gṛhītvā ca dhanaṃ punar āvasthaṃ prāpto jūṭakarṇam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: That wicked man too, following the hole, found it, took the wealth, and then, having regained his former condition, said to <s>Jūṭakarṇa</s>:

children.text: idaṃ tasya tad brahmahṛdayam yasyāsau sāmarthyād aśakyam api sthānam utpatati ||
children.translated_text: "This is that man's very brahma-heart, by whose power he leaps even to a place impossible to reach."
And after dividing half and half, the two sat there at ease.
But I, having fallen into my own decline, thought:

children.text: kadācid ihasthasya me pradīpam ujjvālyāsaṃśayam āsādya māṃ hanyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: "If I stay here, they may perhaps light a lamp, find me without doubt, and kill me."

children.text: iti tasmāt sthānād anyad durgasthānaṃ kṛtavān ||
children.translated_text: So from that place I made another stronghold.

children.text: anye ca ye mamānucarāḥ ta āgatya mām abruvan ||
children.translated_text: And the others who were my followers came and said to me:
"Good <s>Hiraṇya</s>, we who live near you are extremely afflicted by hunger.
We do not have even a mere mouthful.

children.text: astaṃ gate 'pi divase na kiṃcid asmābhir āsāditam ||
children.translated_text: Even though the day has set, we have obtained nothing at all.

children.text: tad arhasy adyāpi tāvad asmān saṃtarpayitum iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore you ought even today at least to satisfy us."

children.text: tathā nāmety uktvāham āvasathaṃ taiḥ samaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Saying, "So be it," I went with them to the dwelling.

children.text: ekāntāvasthitaś ca tayor durātmanoḥ pūrvākhyāte śeṣam ālāpam aśṛṇavam ||
children.translated_text: And, standing apart, I heard the rest of the conversation of those two wicked men, as told before.

children.text: atha jūṭakarṇas tathaivākhyāne vaṃśam cālayati sma ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Jūṭakarṇa</s>, in the same way, shook the bamboo while the story was being told.
He was addressed by the other:

children.text: kim adyāpi nirākṛte tasmin muhurmuhuś cālayasi vaṃśam ||
children.translated_text: "Why, even now when he has been dealt with, do you shake the bamboo again and again?
Keep still.
Enough." For he said:

children.text: bhadra eṣa mamāpakārī mūṣakaḥ punaḥ punar āyāti ||
children.translated_text: "Good sir, this harmful mouse of mine keeps coming again and again."
He laughed and said:
"Do not be afraid.
There is nothing in this.
For:

children.text: bhavaty arthena balavān arthād bhavati paṇḍitaḥ
children.translated_text: A man becomes strong through wealth; through wealth he becomes learned.
Look at this sinful mouse, now reduced to equality with his own kind.
And furthermore:

children.text: yad asyotpatane śaktikāraṇam tad āvayor eva hastagatam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever was the cause of his power to leap is now in the hands of the two of us."
But I approved it just in that way:
"This man speaks the truth.
Today I do not have the power to leap even the breadth of a finger."
And I heard my followers talking among themselves:
"Come, let us go.
Today he is not capable of bending even a blade of grass."

children.text: evam uktvā pañcāśanmātrā gatāḥ punar api pañcaviṃśatiḥ daśa pañca ceti athānye dvādaśāṣṭau ||
children.translated_text: Having said this, about fifty went away; then again twenty-five, ten, and five; then others, twelve and eight.
Then two remained.
And even there one said:

children.text: ayam ātmano 'py udarabharaṇe na samarthaḥ kiṃ punar anyeṣām ||
children.translated_text: "This one is not capable of filling even his own belly, much less those of others."
Saying this, he too went away without concern.

children.text: tato 'haṃ paricintyaitavad iti svam ālayaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, after thinking, "So this is how it is," I went to my own dwelling.

children.text: prabhātasamaye sarva eva sapatnasakāśaṃ gatāḥ daridro 'sāv iti vadantaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At daybreak all of them went to my rival's side, saying, "He is poor."

children.text: tathā pravṛttānām anucarāṇām eko 'pi na matsakāśam āgacchat ||
children.translated_text: Of the followers who had acted in that way, not even one came near me.

children.text: paśyāmi ca māṃ dṛṣṭvā sammukhaṃ ta eva matsapatnaiḥ saha parasparaṃ kilakilāyanto hastāsphālanair mamānucarāḥ saṃkrīḍanti sma ||
children.translated_text: And I saw that those very followers of mine, on seeing me face to face, were playing with my rivals, chattering together and clapping their hands.
And I thought as follows:
"So it is indeed.

children.text: yasyārthās tasya mitrāṇi yasyārthās tasya bāndhavāḥ
children.translated_text: He who has wealth has friends; he who has wealth has kinsmen.

children.text: yasyārthāḥ sa pumāṃl loke yasyārthāḥ sa ca paṇḍitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who has wealth is a man in the world; he who has wealth is learned.
And furthermore:
For a man of little understanding who is deprived of wealth,

children.text: vicchidyante kriyāḥ sarvā grīṣme kusarito yathā ||
children.translated_text: all undertakings are cut off, like small rivers in the hot season.

children.text: tyajanti mitrāṇi dhanair vihīnaṃ putrāś ca dārāś ca suhṛjjanāś ca ||
children.translated_text: Friends abandon one who is without wealth, and so do sons, wives, and dear people.
They take refuge in him again when he has wealth.
For wealth is a man's kinsman in the world.
No one accepts a word spoken even at the right time

children.text: kāle 'py uktaṃ vākyaṃ na kaścit pratipadyate ||
children.translated_text: by a poor man, though he be wise and sweet-spoken.

children.text: caṇḍālaś ca daridraś ca dvāv etau sadṛśau matau
children.translated_text: An outcaste and a poor man: these two are considered alike.

children.text: caṇḍālasya na gṛhṇanti daridro na prayacchati ||
children.translated_text: People do not take from an outcaste; the poor man does not give.

children.text: arthena parihīṇaṃ tu naram aspṛśyatāṃ gatam
children.translated_text: Relatives all abandon a man who is deprived of wealth

children.text: tyajanti bāndhavāḥ sarve mṛtaṃ sattvam ivāsavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and has become untouchable, as the life-breaths abandon a dead being.
A man without wealth is abandoned by friends and kinsmen;
his worldly dealings, wife, and household gone, he is lustreless like one whose life has departed.

children.text: śūnyam aputrasya gṛhaṃ ciraśūnyaṃ yasya nāsti sanmitram
children.translated_text: Empty is the house of a man without a son; long empty is that of one who has no good friend.

children.text: mūrkhasya diśaḥ śūnyāḥ sarvaṃ śūnyaṃ daridrasya ||
children.translated_text: For a fool the directions are empty; for a poor man everything is empty.

children.text: uttiṣṭha kṣaṇam ekam udvaha sakhe dāridryabhāraṃ guruṃ kliṣṭo yāvad ahaṃ ciraṃ maraṇajaṃ seve tvadīyaṃ sukham ||
children.translated_text: "Rise for one moment, friend, and bear the heavy burden of poverty, while I, exhausted for so long, enjoy your happiness born of death."

children.text: ity ukto dhanavarjitena viduṣā gatvā śmaśāne śavo dāridryān maraṇaṃ varaṃ sukhakaraṃ jñātvā sa tūṣṇīṃ sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus addressed in the cremation ground by a learned man bereft of wealth, the corpse, knowing that death was better and more pleasant than poverty, remained silent."
What more, sir?

children.text: na kaścid anyaḥ prativacanam api dadāti ||
children.translated_text: No one else even gives an answer.

children.text: tānīndriyāṇy avikalāni tad eva nāma sā buddhir apratihatā vacanaṃ tad eva
children.translated_text: Those same senses are unimpaired, that same name remains, that intelligence is unobstructed, and that speech is the same;

children.text: arthoṣmaṇā virahitaḥ puruṣaḥ sa eva śete hakāra iva saṃkucitākhilāṅgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: yet, deprived of the heat of wealth, that very man lies like the letter ha, with all his limbs contracted.
Therefore in the world such, for the most part, is the nature of things.

children.text: vinipatitam āryam api janaṃ dṛṣṭvā dhanyandho mūkaś ca bhavati dhanamadāvalepāt ||
children.translated_text: Having seen even a noble man fallen down, a man blinded by wealth becomes mute through the arrogance born of the intoxication of wealth.
And likewise:

children.text: vilocane cāvikale ca vīkṣate sphuṭā ca vāg asti na cāpabhāṣaṇam
children.translated_text: The eyes are unimpaired and he sees; clear speech exists, and there is no impediment in speaking.

children.text: aho nṛśaṃsair vibhavais tathā kṛtaṃ yatheśvaro yācanayantratāṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Ah, by cruel riches he has been made such that a lord has come into the condition of a machine for begging.

children.text: tan mādṛśānāṃ kiṃ nāma tad varaṃ syāt yasya syād īdṛśaḥ phalavipākaḥ yat satataṃ dehīti vakti ||
children.translated_text: Then what indeed could be good for people like me, if it should have such a ripened result, namely that one constantly says, "Give"?

children.text: tat sarvathā dhanahīnasya mamādhunā neha śreyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, in every way, for me who am without wealth there is now no welfare here.
And it has been said:

children.text: vasen mānādhikaṃ sthānaṃ mānahīnaṃ na saṃvaset
children.translated_text: One should dwell in a place where honor is greater; one should not live where honor is lacking.

children.text: mānahīnaṃ suraiḥ sārdhaṃ vimānam api varjayet ||
children.translated_text: Even a heavenly palace, together with the gods, should be avoided if honor is lacking.

children.text: evam uktvāpy ahaṃ punar apy evam acintayam ||
children.translated_text: Even after saying this, I again thought as follows:
Why should I make a request of anyone?
That is even more painful.
For this reason:
For a tree that is crooked, eaten by worms, with bark gnawed away by forest fire,

children.text: taror apy ūṣarasthasya varaṃ janma na cārthinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even if standing in barren soil, birth is better than that of a beggar.
A choking voice in the throat, sweat, pallor and trembling in the face:

children.text: mriyamāṇasya cihnāni yāni tāny eva yācataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the signs that belong to a dying man are the very same for one who begs.
Therefore being a petitioner is also contemptible.

children.text: vairāgyāharaṇaṃ dhiyo 'paharaṇaṃ mithyāvikalpāspadaṃ paryāyo maraṇasya dainyavasatiḥ śaṅkānidhānaṃ param
children.translated_text: It steals away detachment, steals away intelligence, is the abode of false imaginings, another name for death, the dwelling-place of wretchedness, the highest treasury of fears;

children.text: mūrtaṃ lāghavam āspadaṃ ca vipadāṃ tejoharaṃ māninām arthitvaṃ hi manasvināṃ na narakāt paśyāmi vastvantaram ||
children.translated_text: being a petitioner is embodied lightness, the seat of misfortunes, and the remover of the spirit of the proud. For the high-minded, I see no other thing different from hell.
And further:

children.text: nirdravyo hriyam eti hrīparigataḥ prabhraśyate tejaso nistejāḥ paribhūyate paribhavān nirvedam āgacchati
children.translated_text: A man without wealth goes to shame; overcome by shame, he falls away from vigor; without vigor, he is despised; from contempt he comes to disgust.

children.text: nirviṇṇaḥ śucam eti śokamanaso buddhiḥ paribhraśyati nirdhīkaḥ kṣayam ety aho nidhanatā sarvāpadām āspadam ||
children.translated_text: Disgusted, he comes to grief; when his mind is sorrowful, his intelligence collapses; lacking intelligence, he comes to ruin. Ah, poverty is the abode of all calamities.
And further:

children.text: varam ahimukhe krodhāviṣṭe karau viniveśitau viṣam api varaṃ pītvā suptaṃ yamasya niveśane
children.translated_text: It is better to put one's hands into the mouth of an angry snake; it is even better to drink poison and sleep in the abode of <s>Yama</s>;

children.text: girivarataṭād ātmā mukto varaṃ śatadhā gato na tu khalajanāvāptair arthaiḥ priyaṃ kṛtam ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: it is better for one's body to be released from the slope of a great mountain and broken into a hundred pieces, but not to do what is dear to oneself with wealth obtained from base people.

children.text: varaṃ vibhavahīnena prāṇaiḥ saṃtarpito 'nalaḥ nopacāraparibhraṣṭaḥ kṛpaṇo 'bhyarthito janaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is better that fire be satisfied with the life of a man devoid of riches than that a miser, fallen from proper courtesy, be entreated.
Now, when matters stand thus, by what means might there be life?
By theft?
That too, the taking of another's property, is still more painful.
For this reason:

children.text: varaṃ yuktaṃ maunaṃ na ca vacanam uktaṃ yad anṛtaṃ varaṃ mṛtyuḥ ślāghyo na ca parakalatrābhigamanam
children.translated_text: Silence is better than speech that is false; praiseworthy death is better than approaching another's wife.

children.text: varaṃ prāṇatyāgo na ca piśunavākyeṣv abhiratir varaṃ bhikṣārthitvaṃ na ca paradhanāsvādam asakṛt ||
children.translated_text: The giving up of life is better than delight in slanderous words; begging for alms is better than repeatedly tasting another's wealth.
Therefore even in being a petitioner, a man's humiliation is certain.
How so?
A change of outward form, and then the defeat of intelligence;
being a petitioner is like the loss of hope, like another kind of death.
Then shall I sustain myself on food from another?
Painful, sir!
That too is a second door of death.
A sick man, one long away from home, one who eats another's food, one who sleeps in another's dwelling:

children.text: yaj jīvati tan maraṇaṃ so 'sya viśrāmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the fact that he lives is death; death is his rest.
And further:

children.text: jātaḥ kule mahati mānadhanāvaliptaḥ saṃmānanābhyudayakāla iva praharṣī
children.translated_text: Born in a great family, swollen with the wealth of honor, delighted as at the time when respect rises high,

children.text: tac cheṣapiṇḍam api nāma nṛpasya bhuṅkte yaḥ sārameya iva kaṣṭataraṃ kim anyat ||
children.translated_text: if such a man eats even the leftover lump of a king, like a dog, what else is more painful?

children.text: āśāviplutacetaso 'bhilaṣitāl lābhād alābho varas tasyālābhanirākṛtā hi tanutām āpadyate prārthanā
children.translated_text: For a mind overwhelmed by hope, failure to obtain the desired gain is better than obtaining it, for when it is denied by non-obtainment, the request becomes thin and weak.

children.text: iṣṭāvāptisamudbhavas tu sutarāṃ harṣaḥ pramāthī dhṛteḥ setor bhaṅga ivāmbhasāṃ vivaśatāṃ vegena vistāryate ||
children.translated_text: But the joy that arises from attaining what is desired is far more destructive of firmness; like the breaking of a dam by waters, helplessness spreads out with force.
And further:

children.text: tiryakpātitacakṣuṣāṃ smayavatām uccaiḥ kṛtaikabhruvām āḍhyānām avalepatuṅgaśirasāṃ śrutvā giro dāruṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing the harsh words of wealthy men whose eyes are cast sideways, who are full of smirks, who have one eyebrow raised high, and whose heads are lifted high with arrogance,

children.text: kiṃ sadyas sphuṭanaṃ prayuktam urasaḥ sevākṛtām arthinām antas tad yadi varjasāradṛḍhayā nālipyate tṛṣṇayā ||
children.translated_text: why is the immediate bursting of the breast not brought about for servants and petitioners, if within it is not smeared with thirst, firm as the essence of a thunderbolt?

children.text: dīnā dīnamukhair yadi svaśiśukair ākṛṣṭacīrāmbarā krośadbhiḥ kṣudhitair nirannapiṭhirā dṛśyate no gehinī
children.translated_text: If a wife, wretched, with a wretched face, her torn garment pulled by her own children, crying with hunger, and with her cooking-pot empty of food, is seen,

children.text: yācñābhaṅgabhayena gadgadagalaproccāritārdhākṣaraṃ ko dehīti vadet svadagdhajaṭharasyārthe manasvī pumān ||
children.translated_text: what high-minded man, for the sake of his own burned belly, would say "Give," with half-syllables uttered from a choking throat through fear that his request will be refused?
Therefore this poverty is death in many forms.

children.text: atha cet tad eva dhanam ātmīkaromi ||
children.translated_text: But what if I make that very wealth my own?

children.text: mayā tu tayor durātmanor upadhānīkṛtā dṛṣṭapūrvās te dīnārāḥ sthagitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those dinaras, seen before by me, had been hidden, made into a pillow by those two wicked men.

children.text: evaṃ ca sampradhārya gato 'haṃ tam uddeśam ||
children.translated_text: Having decided in this way, I went to that place.

children.text: atha tāv anyamanaskau matvā saṃjighṛkṣur aham upaśliṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, thinking those two were distracted, I drew near, wishing to seize them.
But seeing me, <s>Bṛhatsphig</s> struck me with a club.
I too, wishing to die, somehow turned back.

children.text: punar api cirād baddhāśaḥ samāśvasya dīnārāntikam upaśliṣṭas tena nirdayenaivaṃ śirasy abhihataḥ yenādyāpi svapnagatānām api tādṛśānām udvije ||
children.translated_text: Again, after a long time, full of hope, I took courage and drew near the dinars; but that merciless man struck me on the head in such a way that even today I shrink from such men even in dreams.

children.text: paśya cemaṃ tatkālakṛtaṃ śirasi me vraṇam ||
children.translated_text: And look at this wound on my head, made at that very time.
This too is well said:

children.text: sarvaprāṇavināśasaṃśayakarīṃ prāpyāpadaṃ dustarāṃ pratyāsannabhayo na vetti vidhuraṃ svaṃ jīvitaṃ kāṅkṣati
children.translated_text: When a hard-to-cross calamity is reached, one that threatens the destruction of every living being, a man whose danger is near does not recognize his distressed condition, but longs for his own life.

children.text: uttīrṇas tu tato dhanārtham aparāṃ bhūyo viśaty āpadaṃ prāṇānāṃ ca dhanasya sādhanadhiyām anyonyahetuḥ paṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But when he has crossed beyond it, for the sake of wealth he again enters another danger; for those whose thought is fixed on acquisition, life and wealth are mutually the stake for each other.

children.text: so 'haṃ bahu vicintyāstāṃ dhanam etan mameti nivṛttas tṛṣṇātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: So, after much reflection, I turned away from desire, thinking, 'Let this wealth of mine remain as it is.'
This too is excellently said:

children.text: jñānaṃ cakṣur nedaṃ śīlaṃ kulaputratā na kulajanma
children.translated_text: Knowledge is the eye, not this physical eye; conduct is noble birth, not birth from a noble family.
Contentment is prosperity, and learning is withdrawal from what is irresistible.

children.text: sarvāḥ sampattayas tasya saṃtuṣṭaṃ yasya mānasam
children.translated_text: All riches belong to the man whose mind is content.
For one whose feet are covered with shoes, the whole earth is as if covered with leather.
For one carried along by craving, a hundred yojanas is not far.
For the contented man, there is no regard even for wealth that has come into his hand.

children.text: sarpāḥ pibanti pavanaṃ na ca durbalās te parṇais tṛṇair vanagajā balino bhavanti
children.translated_text: Serpents drink the wind, yet they are not weak; forest elephants become strong on leaves and grass.

children.text: mūlaiḥ phalair munivarāḥ kṣapayanti kālaṃ santoṣa eva mahatāṃ paramā vibhūtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The best sages pass their time on roots and fruits; contentment alone is the supreme splendor of the great.
Therefore, when an object is in every way unattainable, limitation itself is better.

children.text: dāridryasya parā mūrtir yācñā na draviṇālpatā
children.translated_text: Begging is the highest embodiment of poverty, not smallness of wealth.
<s>Śambhu</s> has an old bull as his wealth, and nevertheless he is the supreme lord.
And likewise:

children.text: ko dharmo bhūtadayā kiṃ saukhyam arogatā jantoḥ
children.translated_text: What is <s>dharma</s> (virtue)? Compassion for beings. What is happiness? Health for a living creature.

children.text: kaḥ snehaḥ sadbhāvaḥ kiṃ pāṇḍityaṃ paricchedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What is affection? Goodwill. What is learning? Knowing one's limit.

children.text: santi śākāny araṇyeṣu nadyaś ca vimalodakāḥ
children.translated_text: There are vegetables in the forests, and rivers with clear water.
This moon is a lamp common to all; what use is there for riches?
Thus.

children.text: evam avadhāryāhaṃ svabhavanam āgato 'paśyaṃ citragrīvaṃ pāśabaddham ||
children.translated_text: Having decided in this way, I came to my own dwelling and saw <s>Citragrīva</s> bound in a snare.

children.text: iti ca taṃ mokṣayitvānena laghupatanakenāhaṃ bhavadantikaṃ prāpitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And after freeing him, I was brought here near you by this <s>Laghupatanaka</s>.

children.text: asti kasmiṃścid adhiṣṭhāne somilako nāma kaulikaḥ prativasati sma ||
children.translated_text: In a certain town there once lived a weaver named <s>Somilaka</s>.

children.text: sa yad upārjayati tat tasya divasavyayād ṛte 'dhikatāṃ nopayāti ||
children.translated_text: Whatever he earned did not become more than his daily expenses.
And when he became weary of this, he went to another country.

children.text: tatra mahatā kleśena varṣatrayābhyantare dīnāraśatam arjitam svadeśaṃ ca prāyāt ||
children.translated_text: There, with great hardship, within three years he earned a hundred dinars, and set out for his own country.

children.text: ardhapathe sandhyāsamaye prāpte nyagrodhapādam araṇyamadhye samāsāditavān acintayac ca ||
children.translated_text: Halfway along the road, when evening had arrived, he came upon a banyan tree in the middle of a forest and thought:
Where shall I go now? The village is very far away.

children.text: tad asminn eva nyagrodhapādapa ārūḍho yāminīṃ yāpayāmi ||
children.translated_text: So I will climb this very banyan tree and spend the night here.
Having resolved this, he did so.

children.text: ardharātre ca kathaṃcit svapna iva paśyati sma dvau puruṣau mahāpramāṇau divyākṛtī krodhasaṃraktanayanau tasyābhyāśam āyātau ||
children.translated_text: And at midnight, in some way as if in a dream, he saw two men of great size and divine appearance, their eyes reddened with anger, coming near him.
One of them said:
Ho, <s>Vaṅkālaka</s>, is this how you behave?

children.text: bahuśas tvaṃ mayā nivāritapūrvaḥ yathāsya somilakasya pānabhojanād ṛte 'paraṃ na kiṃcid dātavyam ||
children.translated_text: I have often forbidden you before, saying that nothing is to be given to this <s>Somilaka</s> apart from drink and food.
Today he has a hundred dinars.
Take them away quickly.
Then the other said:
As you command, lord.
I shall do so.

children.text: ity ākarṇya pratibuddho 'sau yāvat dīnāraśataṃ nāpaśyat viṣaṇṇahṛdayaś cācintayat ||
children.translated_text: Hearing this, he awoke; when he did not see the hundred dinars, with a dejected heart he thought:
Alas!
What is this?
How have I been deceived here by some being?

children.text: tat kim adhunā gṛhaṃ gatvā kariṣye ||
children.translated_text: So what shall I do now by going home?

children.text: itaḥ pratinivṛtya punar vittam āsādya yāvad gacchāmi ||
children.translated_text: I will turn back from here, acquire money again, and then go.

children.text: evaṃ cintayan prabhātāyāṃ rātryāṃ bhūyo 'pi nagaram āsādya vittopārjanāya cittam āsthāya katipayakālena pañcāśaddīnārān upārjya punaḥ svadeśagamanāya tenaiva mārgeṇa pravartitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thinking thus, when night had become morning, he again reached the city, fixed his mind on earning wealth, and after some time acquired fifty dinars; then, in order to go back to his own country, he set out by that same road.

children.text: daivacoditaḥ san nādhikaṃ labhate nānyamārgagamanaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: Driven by fate, he did not obtain more, nor did he go by another road.

children.text: tatraiva nīyate yāvad astaṃ gacchati bhānau tam eva nyagrodham āsāditavān acintayac ca ||
children.translated_text: He was led to that very place, and when the sun was setting he reached that same banyan tree and thought:
Alas!
What has this fate-stricken man begun?

children.text: punaḥ sa eva nyagrodharūpī rākṣasa āpatita iti ||
children.translated_text: Again that same demon in the form of a banyan tree has appeared.

children.text: evaṃ cintayan svapnāyamānaḥ paśyati sma dvāvetau puruṣau ||
children.translated_text: Thinking thus, as if dreaming, he saw those same two men.
One of them said:
Ho, <s>Vaṅkāla</s>, <s>Somilaka</s> has fifty dinars.
That is not proper.
Then the other said:
Consider them taken away.
But <s>Somilaka</s>, when he awoke, did not see them; they had been taken.
Then, overcome with despair, he said:
What use have I for life?

children.text: ko 'yaṃ vṛttāntaḥ kena vā kāraṇena mama kleśārjitavittam apaharatīti na vijānāmi ||
children.translated_text: I do not understand what this event is, or for what reason my wealth, earned with toil, is being taken away.
So I shall give up my life.

children.text: evaṃ cintayan nirāhāras tatra eva tasthau yāvat katipayair evāhobhir divyākāraṃ puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭavān ||
children.translated_text: Thinking thus, without food he remained right there, until after only a few days he saw a man of divine appearance.
He said to him:
Ho, <s>Somilaka</s>, I am <s>Dhanada</s>, the giver of wealth.
I do not give wealth to anyone when it is not destined.
And likewise:

children.text: yad abhāvi na tad bhāvi bhāvi yat tad ananyathā
children.translated_text: What is not to be will not come to be; what is to be will not be otherwise.

children.text: iti cintāviṣaghno 'yam agadaḥ kiṃ na pīyate ||
children.translated_text: Why is this antidote, which destroys the poison of anxious thought, not drunk?

children.text: śayāna ākasmikam aśnute phalaṃ kṛtaprayatno 'py aparo 'vasīdati
children.translated_text: One man, lying down, obtains an accidental fruit; another, though he has made effort, sinks down.

children.text: asaṃyamān nṛtyati kevalaṃ jano vidhis tu yatrecchati tatra sampadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: People merely dance from lack of self-control; but wherever fate wishes, there go riches.

children.text: naivākṛtiḥ phalati naiva guṇā na śauryaṃ vidyā na caiva na ca yatnakṛto viśeṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Neither appearance bears fruit, nor virtues, nor valor, nor learning, nor any special distinction produced by effort.

children.text: bhāgyāni karmaphalasañcayasaṃcitāni kāle phalanti puruṣasya yathaiva vṛkṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Fortunes, accumulated as a heap of the fruits of past acts, bear fruit for a man in time, just like trees.

children.text: kruddho 'pi kaḥ kasya karoti duḥkhaṃ sukhaṃ ca kaḥ kasya karoti hṛṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: Who, even when angry, causes suffering to whom? And who, when pleased, causes happiness to whom?

children.text: svakarmagranthigrathito hi lokaḥ kartā karotīti vṛthābhimānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The world is bound by the knot of its own deeds; the conceit, 'the agent acts,' is vain.
Men intelligent, greatly energetic, wise, heroic, and born in good families,

children.text: pāṇipādair upetāś ca pareṣāṃ bhṛtyatāṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and furnished with hands and feet, have gone into servitude to others.
Why lament over this, <s>Somilaka</s>?

children.text: pānabhojanād ṛte tava vittopārjanaṃ na kiṃcid asti ||
children.translated_text: Apart from drink and food, there is no acquisition of wealth for you at all.

children.text: vahanti śibikām anye santy anye śibikāṃ gatāḥ
children.translated_text: Some carry the palanquin, and others are seated in the palanquin.

children.text: akāraṇaṃ hi vaktṛtvaṃ vyutthānaṃ kevalaṃ jarā ||
children.translated_text: For speaking is without cause; rising up is merely old age.
Not by the power and strength of spells, nor by wisdom, nor by manliness,

children.text: avaśyaṃ labhate jantur atra kā paridevanā ||
children.translated_text: does a creature necessarily obtain anything. What lamentation is there in this?

children.text: labdhavyāny eva labhate gantavyāny eva gacchati
children.translated_text: One obtains only what is to be obtained, goes only where one is to go,

children.text: prāptavyāny eva cāpnoti duḥkhāni ca sukhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: and reaches only what is to be reached, both sufferings and pleasures.
Just as unasked-for sufferings come to embodied beings,

children.text: sukhāny api tathā manye daivam atrātiricyate ||
children.translated_text: so too, I think, do pleasures; fate surpasses everything here.

children.text: tat ko viśeṣayati kena kṛto viśiṣṭaḥ ko vā dhanaiḥ saha vijāyati ko daridraḥ
children.translated_text: Who distinguishes anyone, and by whom has one been made distinguished? Who is born together with riches, and who poor?

children.text: bhāgyāni ṣaṭpada iva sthiracañcalāni nityaṃ manuṣyakusumeṣu paribhramanti ||
children.translated_text: Fortunes, steady and unsteady like bees, always wander among the flowers that are human beings.

children.text: tathāpi daivapuruṣayogād arthotpattiḥ puruṣaś carati daivaṃ phalatīti ||
children.translated_text: Still, wealth arises from the conjunction of fate and human effort: the man acts, and fate bears fruit.
In this matter I have been seen by you because you are devoted to exertion.
My appearance is not fruitless.
What shall I do for you?
He made his request:
Give me wealth.
<s>Dhanada</s> laughed and said:
Fool, what will be done with this?
Enjoyment is the point here.

children.text: gaccha asminn evādhiṣṭhāne dvau vaṇijakau paśya ||
children.translated_text: Go; in this very settlement see two merchants.
One is rich, the other is one who enjoys pleasures.

children.text: tau dṛṣṭvā yādṛk tayor abhivāñchasīti tādṛg bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: After seeing them, whatever condition of theirs you desire, such will you become.
Having spoken thus, he disappeared.

children.text: somilako 'pi prabhāte tan nagaraṃ upaviśya sārthavāhaṃ dhanaguptam āsasāda ||
children.translated_text: <s>Somilaka</s>, in the morning, entered that city and approached the caravan-leader <s>Dhanagupta</s>.

children.text: tatrāsau nirbhartsyamāno 'pi kathamapi gṛhe praviśyālindake nipatyāvasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, although he was scolded, he somehow entered the house, lay down in the front hall, and stayed there.

children.text: so 'pi vaṇik sandhyām ativāhya niśāmukhe kiṃcinmātram aśanam akarot ||
children.translated_text: That merchant too, after passing the evening, ate only a little food at the beginning of the night.
He also had a little food given to <s>Somilaka</s>.

children.text: athāsau kaulikaḥ kuśān āstīrya bhūmau nipatya supto 'paśyat tāv eva dvau puruṣau ||
children.translated_text: Then that weaver spread kuśa grass, lay down on the ground, slept, and saw those same two men.
One of them said:

children.text: bho vaṅkāla dhanaguptenādya kaulikasyāśanaṃ dāpayatā dviguṇavyayenātmā niyojita iti ||
children.translated_text: Ho, <s>Vaṅkāla</s>, today, when <s>Dhanagupta</s> had food given to the weaver, his self was assigned to double expenditure.
I calculate everything exactly.

children.text: nāsya sthāpanād ṛte dāne bhojane vā kiṃcid vihitam ||
children.translated_text: For him nothing is ordained in giving or eating, apart from storing.
So I shall set this right in the morning.
After hearing this, he awoke.
<s>Dhanagupta</s> too, in the morning, suffered a great calamity through cholera.
And, tormented by sweating, drinking hot water, and the like, he fasted.
Then that weaver, driven by fate in the morning, thought:
What is the point of wealth like this?
One's nature is hard to abandon.

children.text: tato dvitīyaṃ taṃ vyayaśīlaṃ bhogavarmāṇam uddiśya somilako gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Somilaka</s> went to the second man, that spendthrift <s>Bhogavarman</s>.

children.text: tenāsau mahatā bhojanapānādinā satkṛtaḥ somilakas tathaiva mahati śayane sopacāre svāstīrṇe niśāyāṃ supto 'paśyat tāv eva puruṣau ||
children.translated_text: He was honored by him with abundant food, drink, and the like; and <s>Somilaka</s>, sleeping at night on a fine bed spread well and supplied with comforts, saw those same two men.
One of them said:

children.text: bhadra vaṅkāla śobhanam anuṣṭhitaṃ bhogavarmaṇā prāhuṇakaṃ somilakaṃ saṃmānayatā ||
children.translated_text: Good <s>Vaṅkāla</s>, <s>Bhogavarman</s> has acted well in honoring <s>Somilaka</s> as a guest.
Therefore still more increasing wealth must be given to him for spending and enjoyment.
And he said:
So it shall be done.
When <s>Somilaka</s> awoke, he thought:
Let enjoyments such as these be mine.
What is done with wealth that is only a name?
And likewise he confirmed it:

children.text: asti ahaṃ kadācid yamunākacche śāligrāmamadhye priyakamṛgyām utpannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Once, on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, in the region of <s>Śāligrāma</s>, I was born as a <s>priyaka</s> deer.
We are of six kinds.
And likewise:

children.text: camūraḥ kadalī kandalī priyaka eṇaka ete mṛgayonayaḥ stutāḥ pañca eva ||
children.translated_text: The <s>camūra</s>, <s>kadalī</s>, <s>kandalī</s>, <s>priyaka</s>, and <s>eṇaka</s>: these five alone are praised as deer species.
By the favor of their mother's milk they know two paths:
upward and straight.
These are not caught by hunters.
I am of the <s>priyaka</s> kind, fond of human beings; only after a long time do I close my eyes.

children.text: tathā sati me mātā yadā gatā tadāhaṃ lubdhakaiḥ potaka eva gṛhītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That being so, when my mother had gone away, I, still only a young one, was seized by hunters.

children.text: strīkṣīreṇa vivardhito yāvat tadgṛhe nivasāmi tāvan me mātā svayūthyaiś carati ||
children.translated_text: Raised on a woman's milk, as long as I live in that house, my mother wanders with her own herd.
She said:
Ah, fate!

children.text: aham aputravatī kva me putra iti ||
children.translated_text: I am without a son; how can I have a son?
Hearing this, I understood the matter.
What have I to do with hunters?

children.text: nijakṛtrimayoḥ sahāyayor nijaḥ sahāyo garīyān iti ||
children.translated_text: Of two helpers, one natural and one artificial, the natural helper is weightier.
Then I went freely from the hunter's house.

children.text: atha lubdhakasakāśād āgata iti bhayacakitadṛśaṃ mātaraṃ prāptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having come from the hunter, I reached my mother, whose gaze was terrified and trembling.
By her I was made happy.
When she asked, "What is this wonder?"
I had been reared on breast-milk.
By that, while I was only a six-month-old fawn, I came back to my own herd in extraordinary measure.
Because I had greater speed, as I went I waited for the deer that were coming.

children.text: asmākaṃ dve gatī ūrdhvā āñjasī ca ||
children.translated_text: We have two gaits: the upward one and the straight one.

children.text: tayor mātṛkapayovirahād aham āñjasīṃ vedmi nordhvam ||
children.translated_text: Of these, because I had been without my mother's milk, I knew the straight gait, not the upward one.
Then once I did not see the deer as they were grazing.

children.text: āvignahṛdayaś ca kva te gatā iti vilokitavān ||
children.translated_text: And with an anxious heart I looked about, thinking, "Where have they gone?"

children.text: paśyāmi tān ūrdhvagatyabhijñatayā jālaṃ vilaṅghyāgrato gatān ||
children.translated_text: I saw that, because they knew the upward gait, they had leapt over the net and gone ahead.
But I was ignorant of it, through the fault of a woman's milk.
And so:

children.text: kāryakāle tu samprāpte nāvajñeyaṃ trayaṃ sadā
children.translated_text: When the time for action has arrived, three things should never be despised:

children.text: bījam auṣadham āhāro yathā lābhas tathākrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: seed, medicine, and food, according as they are obtained and according as they are bought.
Because of that medicine called milk, not knowing the upward gait, I escaped by the straight gait and was entangled in the net.

children.text: tataś ca vyādhair durātmabhir jīvagrāhaṃ gṛhītvā krīḍārthaṃ rājaputrāyopanītaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then I was taken alive by wicked hunters and brought to a prince for amusement.

children.text: so 'pi māṃ dṛṣṭvātīva parituṣṭo vyādhān prādeśikena saṃmānitavān ||
children.translated_text: He too, seeing me, was extremely pleased and honored the hunters with a provincial reward.

children.text: māṃ cādareṇāṅgodvartanasnānabhojanadhūpālaṅkāravāsoviśeṣair bhojanaprakāraiś cāsaṃbhāvyaiḥ snigdhadravapeśalaiḥ sakhaṇḍaguḍadāḍimacāturjātakavimiśrair anyaiś ca bhojyair atarpayat ||
children.translated_text: And with care he satisfied me with rubbing of the limbs, baths, food, incense, ornaments, special garments, and unimaginable kinds of food, tender, liquid, and oily, mixed with lumps of sugar, molasses, pomegranate, and the four spices, and with other eatables.

children.text: athāntaḥpurikājanasya rājakumārāṇāṃ ca hastāddhastaṃ ca kautukaparatayā grīvānayanakaracaraṇakarṇāvakarṣaṇaiḥ parasparerṣyābhī rājāṅganābhiḥ sammānaparamparatayā kleśito 'ham ||
children.translated_text: Then, through the curiosity of the women of the inner apartments and the princes, I was passed from hand to hand; by the royal women, out of mutual jealousy and a succession of honors, I was tormented by their pulling at my neck, eyes, hands, feet, and ears.
And I thought:
What use is gold, when it only pains the ear?
Alas, misery!
When shall I reach that forest?

children.text: nivṛttakautukānāṃ ca kadācid vivikte vartamāne rājaputraśayanādhastān mayā prāvṛṭsamaye meghaśabdaśravaṇotkaṇṭhitahṛdayena svayūthacyutena svayūthyān anusmṛtyābhihitam ||
children.translated_text: And once, when their curiosity had subsided and I was in a secluded place beneath the prince's bed, in the rainy season my heart longed at hearing the sound of clouds; separated from my own herd, remembering my herd-mates, I said:
When shall it be for me that I go behind

children.text: pṛṣṭhato yad gamiṣyāmi kadā tan me bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: the herd of deer running, shaken by wind and rain?

children.text: evam uccārayato rājaputreṇa bālabhāvād abhāvitacittenaitāvacchrutvā saṃtrastena dvāḥstho 'bhihitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As I was uttering this, the prince, because of his childish nature and unreflective mind, heard just this much and, terrified, said to the doorkeeper:
By whom was this said?
With his heart tormented, looking all around, he saw me.

children.text: ahaṃ ca lubdhakair mānuṣīṃ vācaṃ śikṣita āsam ||
children.translated_text: And I had been taught human speech by the hunters.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca māṃ mānuṣeṇevānena mṛgenābhihitam vinaṣṭo 'smīti matvā paramāvegaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing me, and thinking, "I am ruined; this deer has spoken as if with a human voice," he fell into the greatest agitation.

children.text: atha kathaṃcid viskhalitavāg asau bahir niścakrāma ||
children.translated_text: Then somehow, his speech faltering, he went outside.
As if possessed by a mighty being, he fell into great illness.

children.text: tatas sarvābhiṣagbhūtatantrikān mahatyā arthamātrayā jvaraparītaḥ prārthitavān evaṃ cābravīt ||
children.translated_text: Then, seized by fever, with a great sum of money he entreated all physicians, exorcists, and tantrikas, and said:

children.text: yo mamaitāṃ rujam apanayati tasyāham akṛśāṃ pūjāṃ kariṣyāmīti ||
children.translated_text: Whoever removes this disease of mine, to him I shall give no small honor.

children.text: aham api tatrāsamīkṣitakāriṇā janena laguḍeṣṭakādibhir druhyamāṇaḥ kenāpi sādhunāvacchannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I too, being harmed there with sticks, bricks, and the like by people acting without examination, was concealed by some good man.
What has this one done?

children.text: atha mamāyuḥśeṣatayā tenāryeṇa sarvalakṣaṇavidā vijñāpito rājaputraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, because some life remained to me, that noble man, who knew all signs, informed the prince:
You have been brought to this condition by people given to thoughtless action.
Again that noble man said as follows:

children.text: priyako nāmaiṣa mṛgo mānuṣīṃ vācaṃ jānāti ||
children.translated_text: This deer, named <s>Priyaka</s>, knows human speech.
He is not a human being.
Good sir, when his mind was awakened by the sound of clouds in the rainy season, he said this out of eager remembrance of his own herd:
"Shaken by wind and rain," and so on.
What is strange in this?

children.text: prāyeṇa pakṣiṇaḥ paśavaś ca bhayāhāramaithunamātravedino bhavanti ity adhigatam eva devena ||
children.translated_text: Your highness has certainly learned that, for the most part, birds and beasts know only fear, food, and mating.
Therefore this one is not superhuman.
And so:
With whatever sort of people one lives, and whatever sort one attends upon,

children.text: yādṛg icchec ca bhavituṃ tādṛg bhavati pūruṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whatever sort one wishes to become, that sort a person becomes.

children.text: hīyate hi naras tāta hīnaiḥ saha samāgamāt
children.translated_text: For a man declines, dear one, through association with the low;

children.text: samaiś ca samatām eti viśiṣṭaiś ca viśiṣṭatām ||
children.translated_text: with equals he reaches equality, and with the distinguished, distinction.

children.text: tat deva manuṣyasamparkāt priyakajātivaśāc ca mānuṣīṃ vācaṃ dadātīti saṃmānitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, your highness, he speaks human speech because of contact with humans and because of the nature of the <s>Priyaka</s> species; thus he was honored.
And so:
Just as a substance on the mountain of sunrise shines through proximity,
so it is said.
What, then, is there here, disconnected from the cause of the fever?
Moreover:

children.text: mantrāṇāṃ parato nāsti bījam uccaraṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: There is nothing beyond mantras, nor likewise seed and utterance;
incoherent prattlings are not able to accomplish the task.
And so:

children.text: śaṅkhaḥ kadalyāṃ kadalī ca bheryāṃ tasyāṃ ca bheryāṃ sumahad vimānam
children.translated_text: A conch in a plantain tree, and the plantain tree in a kettle-drum, and in that kettle-drum a very great aerial palace
That expression, 'the conch, the kettledrum, the plantain, and the aerial car,' became a likeness for an insane suspicion.

children.text: tat kva śaṅkhaḥ kva kadalī kva bherī kva vimānam iti ||
children.translated_text: For where is the conch, where the plantain, where the kettledrum, and where the aerial car?
In just that sort of way, through its incoherence, this has come to apply to you.

children.text: tac ca śrutvāpagatavikāro rājaputraḥ pūrvaprakṛtim āpannaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when he heard that, the prince's derangement departed and he returned to his former nature.

children.text: vicārya tasyāryasya prajñāvibhavaṃ tato mahatīṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā mantrisamīpavartī mantritve kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, after considering the wealth of that noble man's intelligence, the king showed him great honor and made him a minister, one who stayed near the ministers.

children.text: māṃ cāpanīyābhyajya prabhūtenāmbhasā prakṣālitaśarīraṃ kṛtvārakṣipuruṣādhiṣṭhitaṃ tatraiva vane pratimuktavān ||
children.translated_text: And having removed me, anointed me, and washed my body with abundant water, he released me there in that very forest under the supervision of guards.

children.text: tat kiṃ bahunā anubhūtabandhano 'py ahaṃ niyativaśāt punar baddha iti ||
children.translated_text: So, to say no more: although I had experienced bondage before, by the force of fate I have been bound again.
